title: How accurately does the Apple Watch measure your heart rate? We put it to the test
content:
Macworld





With the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, Apple introduced a new health-sensing system. The new energy-efficient LED sensors measure heart rate every five seconds. Heart rate variability is also measured significantly more frequently than before. Macwelt was able to verify this in our review of the Apple Watch Series 12. The watch now measures your pulse every five seconds even when you’re not exercising, and heart rate variability is now recorded every five minutes. The battery still lasts for 24 hours.
This is exciting, because the Apple Watch already had stellar heart-rate tracking. How often and how accurately has the Apple Watch been measuring key health parameters to date? Apple hides the answers to these questions in its support documents. For some measurements, there are no official figures at all. So we took a closer look using the Apple Watch Series 11, which has the same third-gen optical heart rate sensor that was introduced with the Apple Watch Series 6.
How often does the Apple Watch Series 11 measure heart rate?
The answer to this question depends on the situation and the settings on your Apple Watch. In workout mode, the Apple Watch measures your heart rate every five seconds. The watch also measures your heart rate at this high frequency for the first three minutes after your workout. However, there is also a special setting for long workouts, where the user can activate power-saving mode if required. Apple claims that measurements are taken less frequently in this mode. I recorded a HIIT workout using the Polar H10 chest strap as a reference device. I also started the same workout on the Apple Watch Series 11.

				
					

				
			
Heart rate measurement on the Apple Watch Series 11 during a workout.

Foundry




The Apple Watch actually measures heart rate every five seconds while the wearer is exercising. Measurements in power-saving mode during a workout also take place every five seconds. However, the system pauses the measurement for several minutes. This means that the heart rate is measured in short intervals every 5 seconds, then the Apple Watch pauses. You can see this on the graph of the heart rates measured during the workout up to the green line: up to that point, the Apple Watch was running in power-saving mode; after that, I switched it off.
Speaking of power-saving mode. If this mode is activated all the time, no background measurements take place, neither of the heart rate nor of heart rate variability. Furthermore, the vital signs data following a recorded night’s sleep lacks the oxygen saturation readings from during the night.
The Apple Watch can also measure your heart rate every second, just like chest straps do during a workout. However, these measurements only occur sporadically: during user-initiated ECG readings and during background HRV measurements. When you launch the ECG app and place your finger on the Digital Crown, the animation on the Watch and the PDF generated afterwards show the heart rate readings for every second. During HRV measurement, too, the Apple Watch records each heart rate over the course of a minute and then uses a specific formula to calculate the time interval between individual heartbeats.
In the background, and particularly at night while you’re asleep, the Apple Watch measures your heart rate every five minutes. However, the measurements aren’t as regular as they are during exercise. The intervals can vary more significantly when you’re at rest.

		
			


I exported and analysed measurements from a sample night using the Health app. For the sake of clarity, the chart above shows only one hour. During six and a half hours of sleep, the Apple Watch took 83 measurements. The average interval between measurements here is 4 minutes 39 seconds, although gaps of 16 minutes or as little as 40 seconds are also possible.
How accurately does the Apple Watch measure heart rate data?
When unveiling the Apple Watch Series 12, Apple claimed that the new smartwatch was the most accurate heart rate fitness tracker on the market. While we can only verify this claim through a single test, older models show that the Apple Watch was already quite accurate when it came to heart rate measurement.
When we tested the Apple Watch Ultra 3, we found that the Ultra’s readings deviated only very slightly from those of the chest strap. I analysed the same HIIT workout described above using the Apple Watch Series 11. The following picture emerges from the progression of the two graphs. On average, the Apple Watch measures your heart rate quite accurately during exercise. 

		
			


The correlation coefficient between the two measurements–from the Polar H10 and the Apple Watch Series 11–is 0.95. This means the Apple Watch measures quite closely to a chest strap. On average, the two readings differ by just one beat. However, there are outliers: the higher the heart rate, the less accurate the measurement becomes. This can be seen in the line showing heart rates of 160 beats per minute and above. The measurement is also rather inaccurate in power-saving mode, as the Apple Watch can completely miss heart rate spikes due to the sporadic mode.
The new features Apple announced for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are exciting because they effectively turn the entire heart rate measurement algorithm on its head.

title: Apple May Cancel OLED iMac
content:
Apple is considering delaying or scrapping its planned iMac with an OLED display amid concerns about high panel costs and weaker-than-expected demand for ‌OLED‌ devices, according to The Elec.


Citing industry sources, the Korean publication says Apple is discussing changes to the ‌OLED‌ ‌iMac‌'s development schedule with Samsung Display. The company could put the project on hold altogether, although one industry official said the talks are currently focused on delaying it while Apple determines demand. 

2029 or 2030. Apple has now reportedly asked LCD suppliers, including BOE, to develop panels for a new ‌iMac‌ expected around 2029, suggesting it could stick with LCD technology through the period originally planned for the ‌OLED‌ upgrade.

Rising memory costs are reportedly adding to the expense of bringing ‌OLED‌ to more of Apple's products.

iPad Pro demand is reportedly another factor. The 2024 models introduced brighter tandem ‌OLED‌ displays, but higher prices appear to have discouraged many buyers. By October that year, Apple had reportedly cut its shipments from as many as 10 million units to 6.7 million.

Samsung Display and LG Display are forecast to ship a combined 4.9 million ‌iPad Pro‌ ‌OLED‌ panels in 2026, down approximately 18% from six million in 2025. Samsung's shipments are expected to fall from 2.1 million to 1.5 million panels, while LG's are projected to drop from 3.9 million to 3.4 million.

The Elec suggests the review may also reflect Apple's change in leadership. Since John Ternus became CEO in September, Apple has reportedly been reassessing whether the benefits of expensive ‌OLED‌ panels justify their cost.

approached display suppliers about the ‌OLED‌ ‌iMac‌ in 2025, seeking a 24-inch panel with 600 nits of brightness and a pixel density of 218 pixels per inch.

Samsung Display is believed to have been developing a panel at roughly 220 pixels per inch for the device on its existing large-format quantum dot ‌OLED‌ production lines. The design uses five light-emitting layers to improve brightness and lifespan, and Samsung had planned to send Apple samples in the second half of 2026.

five light-emitting layers, but development of its panel for the first ‌OLED‌ ‌iMac‌ has reportedly stopped.

content:

Plug your MacBook in and out of a multi-port laptop docking station to swiftly add multiple devices and external displays with just one cable connection to your laptop. We tested the top contenders to find the best Thunderbolt and USB-C docks available to owners of the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro. MacBook Neo users can use any of these docks but are limited to a 10Gbps bandwidth and some display limitations.  
Thunderbolt, USB4 or USB-C
The connectors all look the same (technically known as a “Type-C connector”), but there are significant differences, particularly on speed that will determine both data-transfer rate and higher external display refresh rates.
USB-C: 5Gbps or 10Gbps
USB4: 20Gbps or 40Gbps
Thunderbolt 3 and 4: 40Gbps
Thunderbolt 5: 80Gbps / 120Gbps
Our list Which ports does my MacBook have will show you how many USB-C or more likely one of Thunderbolt 3, 4 or 5 that you have.
While a Thunderbolt 4 (TB4) dock will be enough for most casual users, if you can stretch the budget go for a TB5 dock as it will remain current for years, saving you money in the long term, and is backwards compatible with earlier versions and all the way back to USB-C. High-end professionals should always aim for Thunderbolt 5.
The dock needs one (“upstream“) Thunderbolt or USB-C port for connecting to and charging your laptop (although all recent MacBooks can also power via the MagSafe 3 port), and at least another (“downstream“) to attach further devices (hard drives, external display, and others).
The USB-C MacBook Neo has just the one data port, with the other reserved for charging. A dock with Power Delivery will greatly expand the entry-level Mac laptop.
For more detail, read our Thunderbolt 5 vs Thunderbolt 4 vs Thunderbolt 3 vs USB4 explainer.
Add external displays to your MacBook
If you use your laptop as your principal computer, attaching at least one larger display to create a hybrid desktop/laptop setup, with a keyboard and mouse, will boost your productivity. You can turn that 13in MacBook’s cramped screen real-estate into an iconic iMac-sized 27in or even larger screen by adding an extra display—or connect two or even four large monitors to extend your screen across your whole desk. Take a look at our recommended best monitors and displays for Mac and also the best portable monitors for Mac.
You’ll get two or more Extended mode screens (where the screen extends beyond what you can see on the laptop screen) using a Thunderbolt connection (or DisplayPort/HDMI). Natively over mere USB-C, Macs can connect to only one external display in Extended mode, as opposed to Mirrored mode (which replicates exactly what you get on the laptop screen) but DisplayLink is third-party software that allows some docks to extend to up to four screens on even the most basic Mac. DisplayLink-supporting docks are also the only way that non-Pro/Max M1 and M2 MacBooks can connect more than one external display.
More explained: we cover more on Mac docking stations and external displays at the end of this feature below our recommendations.
Do I need a docking station?
With three TB4 or TB5 and an HDMI port, a MacBook with a Max chip could connect to up to four external displays without the need for a dock, although such a power user would likely require extra Thunderbolt and other ports for more devices to make up for using all the laptop ports for multiple monitors. See below our list of recommended docking stations for more detail on the external display options with each recent MacBook.
All docks come with a bunch of USB ports: some old-school USB-A and newer, more capable USB-C. MacBook Pros also have an SD card reader. Although this card reader is rated as UHS-II (312MBps), Apple has pegged it back at 250MBps, so for the fastest speeds (and a microSD slot if you need one), a dock will likely be a better choice for memory-card use if it is rated at UHS-II rather than UHS-I (104MBps).
MacBooks also lack wired Internet access via an Ethernet port, so if you want to escape flaky Wi-Fi, buy a dock with at least Gigabit Ethernet, although you could add a Thunderbolt-to-Ethernet adapter instead if you have a spare TB port. Some later docks include faster 2.5Gb, 5Gb or even 10Gb Ethernet but you’ll need a supporting router or other device to get the benefits, although these faster Ethernet ports are backwards compatible with Gigabit so will future-proof your purchase.
While docking stations are most often attached to MacBooks, they can be useful with a desktop Mac. The Mac mini especially can benefit from the extra ports and built-in SSD slot options. We cover these specifically in our feature on how to upgrade the Mac mini, including reviews of the best hubs and docks that fit the mini. 
Dock or hub?
If you need just a few extra ports, a USB-C hub or Thunderbolt hub might be your best choice—see our roundup of the best USB-C and Thunderbolt hubs for Mac. However, if you require a bunch of fast ports including Gigabit (or faster) Ethernet and multiple video ports plus more powerful charging capability, then look for a full dock that fulfils your needs. We’ve reviewed the best hubs alongside the docks.

USB PD: Power Delivery for your laptop
Most docks can charge the connected MacBook, so look for the right Power Delivery (PD) rating that suits your laptop. You can’t over-power a MacBook so the simplest advice is to aim as high as you can. 70W will be more than enough to fast-charge a MacBook Air but go for 85W or more (PD 3.0) for a MacBook Pro, and 140W (PD 3.1) for the top-end 16-inch Pro.

Which ports are on each MacBook?
Of Apple’s recent laptop ranges, the M1/M2/M3 MacBook Air and 14-inch M3 MacBook Pro feature two ports that Apple specified as “Thunderbolt / USB 4” ports, while more recent the 13in and 15in M4/M5 MacBook Air models feature two Thunderbolt 4 ports. The 14in and 16in M1/M2/M3 Pro, plain M4/M5 MacBook Pro, and M1/M2/M3 Max MacBook Pro models come with three Thunderbolt 4 (TB4) ports. Ignore Apple’s dual designation of non-4 Thunderbolt and USB4—it just means that the ports don’t certify as pure Thunderbolt 4, and that shouldn’t worry most users except for the number of external displays each supports.
Apple’s latest M4/M5 Pro and M4/M5 Max MacBook Pro models feature three of the latest Thunderbolt 5 ports, which are backwards compatible with TB4, TB3 and USB-C. They promise 80Gbps data transfer and 120Gbps video rates. Until the technology finds its way into more devices and the Thunderbolt 5 dock market matures, you are still going to do very well with a 40Gbps Thunderbolt 4 dock, but Thunderbolt 5 docks are fast becoming the norm for new releases.
Thunderbolt 5 frees the latest top-end M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBooks from the two-display limitation forced on them by the macOS’s lack of MST (Multi Stream Transport) support. The M5 Pro now supports up to three external displays over a single Thunderbolt connection and the M5 Max up to four. To reach four external displays most docks reviewed here would need to daisy-chain the fourth display off one of the others.
The entry-level MacBook Neo utilizes lower-spec USB-C rather than Thunderbolt, with 10Gbps rather than Thunderbolt’s 40Gbps or 80Gbps. A USB-C dock is therefore all you should need but it will work with Thunderbolt, which is backwards compatible, but limited to the Neo’s 10Gbps bandwidth.

13-inch and 15-inch M1/M2/M3 MacBook Air: Two Thunderbolt/USB4 ports and one MagSafe 3 charging port, plus headphone jack
13-inch and 15-inch M4/M5 MacBook Air: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports and one MagSafe 3 charging port, plus headphone jack
13-inch M1/M2 MacBook Pro: Two Thunderbolt/USB4 ports and one MagSafe 3 charging port, plus headphone jack
14-inch M3 MacBook Pro: Two Thunderbolt/USB4 ports, one HDMI port, one SDXC card slot, plus headphone jack
14-inch M1/M2/M3 Pro, M1/M2/M3 Max and plain M4/M5/M6 MacBook Pro: Three Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports, one HDMI port, one SDXC card slot, plus headphone jack
14-inch M4/M5 Pro or M4/M5 Max MacBook Pro: Three Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) ports, one HDMI port, one SDXC card slot, plus headphone jack
16-inch M1/M2/M3 Pro or M1/M2/M3 Max MacBook Pro: Three Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports, one HDMI port, one SDXC card slot, plus headphone jack
16-inch M4/M5 Pro or M4/M5 Max MacBook Pro: Three Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) ports, one HDMI port, one SDXC card slot, plus headphone jack
How many external displays can each MacBook support without a dock?
Neo: One external display with up to 4K resolution at 60Hz. Use a DisplayLink dock for more than one monitor on the MacBook Neo.
M1/M2: One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz. Use a DisplayLink dock for more than one monitor on these MacBooks.
M3: Supports up to two external displays, one with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz and one at 5K/60Hz when the MacBook lid is closed.
M4: Supports up to two external displays, one with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz and one at 5K/60Hz.
M5: Supports up to two external 6K/60Hz or 4K/144Hz displays, or one 8K/60Hz, 5K/120Hz, 4K/240Hz.
M6: Supports up to two external 6K/60Hz or 4K/165Hz displays, or one 8K/60Hz, 5K/120Hz, 4K/240Hz.
M1/M2/M3/M4 Pro: Up to two external displays with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz over Thunderbolt, or one external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz over Thunderbolt and one external display with up to 4K resolution at 144Hz over HDMI. Or one external display supported at 8K resolution at 60Hz or one external display at 4K resolution at 240Hz over HDMI.
M1/M2/M3/M4 Max: Up to four external displays: Up to three external displays with 6K resolution at 60Hz over Thunderbolt and one external display with up to 4K resolution at 144Hz over HDMI. Up to three external displays: Up to two external displays with 6K resolution at 60Hz over Thunderbolt and one external display with up to 8K resolution at 60Hz or one external display with 4K resolution at 240Hz over HDMI.
M5 Pro: Supports up to three external displays over a single Thunderbolt port. Up to three displays up to a native resolution of 6K (6144 x 3456) at 60Hz or 4K (3840 x 2160) at 144Hz over Thunderbolt or HDMI. Or one external display supported at 8K (7680 x 4320) at 60Hz, 5K (5120 x 2880) at 120Hz, or 4K (3840 x 2160) at 240Hz, plus a second display up to a native resolution of 5K (5120 x 2880) at 120Hz or 4K (3840 x 2160) at 200Hz over Thunderbolt or HDMI.
M5 Max: Supports up to four external displays over a single Thunderbolt port. Up to four displays up to a native resolution of 6K (6144 x 3456) at 60Hz or 4K (3840 x 2160) at 144Hz over Thunderbolt or HDMI. Two displays up to a native resolution of 8K (7680 x 4320) at 60Hz, 5K (5120 x 2880) at 120Hz, or 4K (3840 x 2160) at 240Hz over Thunderbolt or HDMI.
Mac docking stations and external displays

				
					

				
			
Baseus




While Apple’s MacBooks featuring the company’s own M-series Silicon chips are super speedy compared to the models sporting Intel processors, models with plain (non-Pro or -Max) M1 and M2 chips come with an incredible limitation: they don’t support more than one external display in Extended Mode even via their Thunderbolt ports. Plain M3 MacBooks can support two displays but only with their lids closed. The MacBook Neo uses a different A18 Pro chip and has the same single-monitor limitation as the plain M1 and M2.
This limitation means that when using any docking station, M1/M2 and Neo MacBook users cannot extend their desktop over two or more displays, and will be limited to either dual Mirrored displays or one external display—although adding third-party DisplayLink or InstantView software to the Mac and connecting to a dedicated USB-C dock will allow you to add more than one external monitor to an M1, M2 or M3 MacBook. Follow that link for our roundup of the best USB-C DisplayLink docks, and we’ve included our favorite in our roundup above.
In the example above, standard M1/M2/Neo Macs would require DisplayLink to achieve Extended Mode 2. M1/M2/M3/M4 Pro/Max and standard M3/M4/M5 onwards can natively work in that mode without DisplayLink but would require it for three or more extended screens. M5 Pro supports three screens, and M5 Max supports four, without requiring DisplayLink.
Above, we’ve listed the native external display options for each MacBook. Thunderbolt 5 docks should support up to four 6K displays if you own an M5 Max-chip MacBook Pro.
While some docking stations promise support for 8K displays, Macs are limited to 6K support via the dock. Macs with an M2/M3/M4 Pro or Max chip can support an 8K display at 60Hz but only when it is connected via the Mac’s own HDMI port and not any port on the dock.
Dock, hub or dongle: Whole lotta ports
You need one (“upstream“) Thunderbolt or USB-C port for connecting to and charging your laptop (although the 14/16in MacBooks can also power via the MagSafe port), and likely at least another (“downstream“) to attach further devices (hard drives, external display, and others).
There are many inexpensive USB-C dongles/hubs that let you add more devices to a MacBook (see our roundup of the best USB-C adapters for Macs) or a Thunderbolt hub offering a few extra ports might be all your need, but for maximum flexibility check out a docking station that takes care of all your extra port requirements, and allows you to simply attach it to your laptop with just one cable when you get to the office or come home.
Docks aren’t just for MacBooks. Mac mini (2018 and later) and iMac (2017 and later) owners may also consider expanding their ports with a Thunderbolt docking station.
The inclusion of an SD or microSD card reader isn’t just for camera buffs. It’s a convenient and affordable way to add storage to your laptop setup. We found a 512GB Samsung Evo microSD card on Amazon for around $100 in the US and under £100 in the UK. That’s a very cheap way of adding half a terabyte of portable storage. For more details read up on our best microSD cards.
Some of the docks reviewed above include an integrated SSD enclosure that lets you add up to 8TB of fast storage to your connected MacBook.
Charging the laptop
While the MacBook Neo can get by on 20W Power Delivery (PD), the M1/M2/M3/M4/M5 MacBook Air requires a PD charger with at least 30W power, but you can fast-charge an M2 and later Air with a charger rated at over 70W. You’ll need 67W for the 13-inch MacBook Pro and 70W for the 14-inch MBP (with 8-, 10-, 11-or 12-core CPU), 96W for 14-inch MBP (with 12- or 14-core CPU), and 96W (preferably 140W) for the 16-inch MBP. The older 15in MacBook Pro requires a 87W PD charger.
If you own a larger MacBook Pro, buy a dock with a PD (Power Delivery) potential of at least 85W if you can. USB PD 3.0 maxes at 100W, while USB PD 3.1 can support up to 240W of power. The 16-inch MacBook Pro requires 140W to fast-charge, so owners of that laptop should look for a PD 3.1 charger.
If you just need a spare charger, we’ve tested the best MacBook chargers for you.
Other dock options
Here we concentrate on Thunderbolt docks, but also include cheaper USB-C docks—which Thunderbolt MacBooks can use, but at the cost of reduced bandwidth and display limitations. We’ve also included our favorite Thunderbolt hubs for smaller and cheaper alternatives. For more non-Thunderbolt USB-C-only docks check out Tech Advisor’s roundup of the best USB-C docking stations for laptops. Tech Advisor also reviews all the available Thunderbolt 4 docks.
Now think about a stand to go alongside the dock
These MacBook docking stations look and work great with a laptop stand, and we’ve also tested some MacBook-friendly stands that lack all the extra ports but keep your MacBook/Air/Pro upright and out of the way: further saving valuable desk space, reducing clutter, keeping your laptop cool, and saving it from spills.

Apple gives gift cards with selected purchases rather than lowering prices. It is worth waiting for Apple’s Black Friday if you are likely to want to spend more money at Apple because in some cases the value of the gift cards could be better than the discount you see elsewhere. 
However, the Black Friday period is one of the strongest periods for Apple deals, alongside Prime Day and other sales. We therefore recommend that you consider an early offer if it is close to that model’s previous low; stock and popular configurations can run out, and the biggest reductions often apply to older or clearance models.
In short: Compare retailer discounts with the value of Apple’s gift card before deciding. Treat the card as its full face value only if it covers spending you already planned, and compare the exact same model and configuration.

 FAQ 


1.
Does Apple do a Black Friday sale?
Apple doesn’t typically reduce prices for Black Friday. We wish it would, but instead, Apple typically runs a Black Friday-to-Cyber Monday shopping event during which eligible purchases come with an Apple gift card.





2.
When do the Black Friday sales begin? 
Black Friday officially begins on the day after Thanksgiving, which in 2026 is Friday, November 27. However, the sales begin well before that–we saw deals starting at the beginning of November. The main event runs through the weekend and concludes on Cyber Monday, which is November 30.





3.
Should I wait for Cyber Monday to purchase?
While it’s always possible that a better deal is waiting around the corner, if you see a good deal, don’t wait. While Cyber Monday promises impressive deals there’s always the risk that the Apple device you want sells out and you miss out on the great deal everyone else got.





4.
Are Apple’s Black Friday gift cards worth it?
Apple’s gift-card offers give you extra value on an eligible purchase rather than an immediate price cut.
A key benefit is flexibility: you can put the card toward another Apple product or services and digital purchases, such as subscriptions and App Store purchases.
That flexibility is most valuable if you expect to spend more with Apple. A gift card doesn’t lower the price you pay for the qualifying item, and it may be less appealing if you don’t plan to buy anything else from Apple; competing retailers may offer direct discounts instead.





5.
Can I use the gift card toward the product I’m buying?
No. The gift card can only be used for future purchases. You can’t use the gift card to reduce the overall cost of the qualifying purchase.





6.
What can I buy with an Apple Gift Card?
An Apple Gift Card is remarkably versatile – it can be used to buy almost anything Apple sells, including hardware, services, subscriptions, and digital content.
This means you can use the balance toward:
Physical Apple products: iPhones, iPads, Macs, Apple Watches, AirPods, HomePods, Apple TV, and accessories like the Apple Pencil or Magic Keyboard.
Apple services and subscriptions: Apple Music, Apple TV+, iCloud storage, Apple Arcade, and Apple News+.
Digital content: movies, music, games, apps, and in-app purchases from the App Store, iTunes Store, and Apple Books
The card can be redeemed to your Apple Account, and the balance never expires. It’s accepted at the Apple Store (online and in retail locations), the App Store, and across Apple’s digital storefronts.





7.
What happens to my Apple Black Friday gift card if I return the product?
If you return a product purchased during Apple’s Black Friday promotion, you’ll also need to return the accompanying gift card to receive a full refund. If you’ve already redeemed the gift card, or don’t return it, Apple will deduct its value from your refund.
For example, if you buy an eligible MacBook Pro with a $300 gift card and subsequently return the MacBook without returning the gift card, Apple will deduct $300 from the refund.





8.
Where can I get the best Black Friday deals? 





Spotting a good Black Friday deal takes a bit of work but we’ll be doing most of it for you. We’ll be tracking the best Black Friday Apple deals throughout November, highlighting worthwhile discounts on Macs, iPads, iPhones, Apple Watches and AirPods.

title: How to use NotProton to unlock Windows game compatibility in Steam for Mac

NotProton lets Mac owners install and play Windows games through the native Steam client without installing Windows. Here's how to set it up and what worked on our M3 MacBook Air.

Running Windows games on Mac
Steam for Mac normally won't let you install Windows-only games, but NotProton offers a way around that limitation. We used it to launch two Windows games, including a 3D title whose Mac version no longer works on modern macOS releases.
Both games launched with functioning graphics, audio, and controls, although one eventually froze. Getting everything running also required some troubleshooting with CrossOver and macOS permissions.

title: Instagram Now Lets You Save Songs to Apple Music

title: Apple’s 2027 anniversary iPhone 20 rumors, specs and release date
content:
Macworld





The original iPhone was previewed in January 2007 and then released on June 29, 2007. So in 2027, it will turn 20 years old, and rumors point to Apple commemorating the event with a special 20th-anniversary model.
It’s not expected to launch on June 29 (it will probably be in September, as usual), and it may not be a special one-off product, but rather the next major evolution of the iPhone, much like the iPhone X in 2017. But either way, the big two-oh is supposed to bring something really special.
Will Apple call its next-generation models iPhone 19, or skip straight to iPhone 20 to mark the anniversary? Reports suggest the latter is possible, but the name remains unconfirmed. 
Here’s what we’ve gleaned from the rumors and leaks so far.
20th Anniversary iPhone: What to expect
Name: Unconfirmed; one report suggests Apple could skip iPhone 19 and use iPhone 20.
Major redesign: Apple is expected to mark the iPhone’s 20th anniversary in 2027 with a near-all-screen design, curved glass, ultra-thin bezels, and two Pro-sized models.
Display upgrades: Face ID could move under the display, leaving only a small punch-hole front camera for a cleaner look.
Key hardware improvements: Rumored upgrades include a new Sony camera sensor, solid-state haptic buttons, and a silicon-anode battery for better battery life.
More powerful internals: The phone is expected to feature a next generation chip; a C3 modem, and improved wireless connectivity for better performance and efficiency.
Timing and price: A fall 2027 launch is expected with a price of $1,299 or more.


Will Apple skip iPhone 19 and launch iPhone 20?

				
					

				
			
Steve Jobs demonstrating  the first iPhone in January 2007.

Apple




The iPhone that launches in 2027 will mark twenty years since the first iPhone was announced. What will this 20th-anniversary iPhone be called? iPhone 20 is one reported possibility, while iPhone XX remains a speculative alternative.
In October 2025, research firm Omdia reportedly predicted that Apple would skip the iPhone 19 name and move directly to iPhone 20. 
There is a precedent. For the iPhone’s tenth anniversary in 2017, Apple introduced the iPhone 8 and iPhone 8 Plus alongside the iPhone X, skipping iPhone 9 entirely. The iPhone X brought an OLED display with no Home button, Face ID, and a then-record starting price of $999. It also supported wireless charging, which debuted on the iPhone 8 models that year.
Apple could take a similar approach in 2027, launching a standard iPhone 19 alongside a more expensive anniversary model called iPhone 20 – or another name entirely. The 2017 launch shows that Apple can depart from its numbering sequence, but neither the anniversary model’s name nor the possibility of an iPhone 19 launching alongside it is confirmed.






iPhone 19 or 20 release date: When will the 20th Anniversary iPhone launch?
Likely release date: September 2027
There has been no hard information on the 20th Anniversary iPhone’s release date yet, but it is generally expected to launch in the typical time frame for iPhones: an announcement in September and an on-sale in late September or October 2027.
An August 2026 report from a financial analyst at Jefferies claimed that Apple had canceled the all-glass anniversary iPhone because of manufacturing difficulties and concerns about its financial viability. However, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman disputed that report, saying Apple was still planning a glass-centric redesign for 2027, albeit with changes to its construction.






How much will the 20th Anniversary iPhone cost?
High starting price estimated at $1,299 or more
It’s too early to predict what the RAM crunch will do to next year’s prices, but we expect the 20th Anniversary iPhone to be expensive. With more advanced technology than most “Pro” iPhones, the starting price will likely be at least $1,299, if not more.






What will the 20th Anniversary iPhone look like?
Two sizes with slightly larger displays rumored
Edge-to-edge displays
Curved glass design
One of the defining visual characteristics of the 20th Anniversary iPhone will reportedly be its all-display look. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman claimed in May 2025 that Apple is planning an all-glass design.  Leaks have described the handset as having “a quad-curved screen design,” with the idea being that the phone will appear to be one big display. Bezels could be minimized to the point where you don’t even see them, and the glass will curve down on all four sides. It’s been reported that Apple could adopt its Liquid Glass branding as well.
“Glass-centric” doesn’t necessarily mean an entirely glass enclosure. According to Gurman’s August 2026 report, Apple encountered difficulties joining the front and back glass panels when preparing the design for mass production. The revised approach reportedly uses a metal band to connect them, while retaining glass that curves around all four sides.
A prominent leaker by the name of Ice Universe on Weibo says Apple is testing two designs, with two sizes for each. One design has a flat back, the other has a curved-glass back. Apple has been refining the curve of that model over time, but it’s not clear which one will go into production.
Reports also suggest that Apple is preparing two anniversary models with slightly larger displays than the current Pro iPhones. According to leaker Digital Chat Station in July 2026, Apple is testing a 6.41-inch display with a resolution of approximately 2,686 × 1,236 pixels and a 6.96-inch display with approximately 2,912 × 1,340 pixels. The larger model could be marketed as having a 7-inch screen, potentially making it the largest display on a conventional, non-folding iPhone.






Will the 20th Anniversary iPhone have a Dynamic Island?
Under-display Face ID expected
Hole-punch camera for selfie cam rumored

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




One of the persistent rumors over the past several years is that Apple will continue to put more front camera system components under the display, until it’s all display with no cutouts at all.
That may be several years away, but at least some of the components might be able to go behind the OLED display. One rumor claims that Apple will use a “spliced micro-transparent glass,” which will allow it to put the IR emitter under the display, leaving just the regular camera and maybe the IR receiving camera in a cutout region. If the IR camera can effectively go under the display as well, the 20th Anniversary iPhone will have just a single round punch-hole camera in front but retain Face ID.
The Digital Chat Station leak from July 2026 also indicated that Apple is testing a smaller Dynamic Island-style hole-punch design. 
Analyst Ross Young suggested in a post on X back in January 2026 that a smaller Dynamic Island would remain through 2027. He believes Apple’s 2028 iPhone Pro models will feature a centered hole-punch cutout in the display.






What camera will the 20th Anniversary iPhone have?
Custom LOFIC image sensor rumored
Triple-camera array with telephoto lens

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




According to a Korean-language blog post by a leaker who goes by yeux1122 (who has been accurate in the past with some supply-chain scoops), Apple is working together with Sony on a custom image sensor that uses LOFIC (Lateral Integral Overflow Capacitor) technology.
Phone makers Honor, Xiaomi, and Huawei all use sensors with LOFIC technology in their flagship phones now. It’s a technique that allows sensors to capture low-light or dark areas of an image with less noise, along with brighter areas of an image, without increasing ISO sensitivity. In other words, it gives the camera more dynamic range with less noise.
Otherwise, we expect the 20th Anniversary iPhone to have a triple-camera system like the current Pro models, with wide, ultrawide, and telephoto cameras. It’s likely that the cameras will have significant upgrades, however, with a possible 200MP sensor.






Will the 20th Anniversary iPhone have physical buttons?
Solid-state with haptics could replace physical buttons

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




On all current MacBooks (other than MacBook Neo), the trackpad doesn’t actually move. Instead, it produces the sensation of being clicked using precise haptic feedback. It’s very effective and reduces the possibility of breakage due to fewer moving parts.
The 20th Anniversary iPhone is supposed to replace the power, volume, Action, and Camera Control buttons with parts that operate in a similar way. These buttons wouldn’t move at all. Rather, they will be integrated into the frame itself, but will have touch capacitors and haptics to give them the feel of an actual button.
Weibo account Instant Digital (with a mixed track record) says extensive testing is ongoing to make sure these new solid-state haptic buttons work well with gloves, cases, wet hands, and so on. 
If Apple can pull this off and they feel as good as real buttons, it will be an important part of the durability of the new iPhone. With the display glass curving down on all edges, the edge area of the frame itself will be very thin, and further cutouts to accommodate buttons would make it less likely to resist bending.






What specs will the 20th Anniversary iPhone 19 or 20 have?
A next-generation A-series processor is expected
A C3 modem has been rumored
RAM capacity remains unconfirmed
The 20th-anniversary iPhone is expected to feature a successor to the iPhone 18 Pro’s A20 Pro processor, potentially called A21 Pro. Apple has not announced the chip or its specifications.
Reports have suggested that Apple’s C3 cellular modem could arrive in 2027. The C2 is already used in the iPhone 18 Pro worldwide and in the iPhone 18 Pro Max outside the U.S.; the U.S. Pro Max uses Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80. Whether C3 will appear in every anniversary model remains unconfirmed.
Apple’s N1 wireless chip supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. It is too early to say whether the anniversary iPhone will retain N1 or introduce a successor.
RAM capacity is also unknown. Based on the iPhone 18 Pro, we would expect at least 12GB, while 16GB is a possibility if future features require more memory. This is our assessment rather than a confirmed specification or a sourced claim of a RAM increase.






Will the 20th Anniversary iPhone have longer battery life?
New battery technology
A report from ETNews in 2025 said that Apple is looking to use a battery with a pure silicon anode in the 20th Anniversary iPhone.
A silicon anode could increase energy density, allowing Apple to fit more battery capacity into the same space or use a smaller battery without sacrificing capacity. Some Android phones already demonstrate the potential of silicon-based batteries: the Oppo Find X9 Pro, for example, has a 7,500mAh silicon-carbon battery. That is different from the pure-silicon anode technology reportedly being considered for Apple’s anniversary iPhone. Apple’s battery capacity remains unknown, and any improvement in battery life would also depend on the display, processor, modem, and software.

The Apple Watch Series 12 has been out for a couple of months, and the best discount we’ve seen lately has been $10 or $20. Ahead of Black Friday, Apple’s newest smartwatch dropped to $329, a savings of $70 off its MSRP. That’s the best price we’ve ever seen, even lower than the $50 savings during the fall Prime Day, so now’s your chance to get your hands on this product.
The Apple Series 12 comes with a ton of sensors that will come in handy in your day-to-day activity. The heart sensor will read your heart rate every five seconds, which is far more frequently than previous models. Mix that in with your sleep score and activity, and you get a score every day so you know how much energy you have to tackle the day. Battery life on this smartwatch is great too. Apple claims 24 hours on a single charge, but we actually found it delivered a much better performance. In our tests, we used the Series 12 for 45.5 hours before it needed a recharge, which is impressive, but a bit below the 47.5 hours the Series 11 delivered.
You’ll get a few exclusive features with this newest model as well. There are the new Audio Intelligence features, including Siri Recap and Live Rewind, that provide summaries of conversations, the new Health app and Readiness score; as well as faster Siri AI thanks to the new S11 chip. It’s truly a fantastic smartwatch, whether you’re new to Apple Watch or upgrading from an earlier model.

Apple today refreshed its suite of Creator Studio apps, launching the fall updates that it announced in October.


Final Cut Pro with MotionVFX integration is now available, letting users access MotionVFX templates, titles, themes, effects, layouts, and more right in Apple's video editing app. Timeline clips can be disconnected from the primary storyline, and there are new keyframe easing options. Sidecar support for turning the iPad into a multi-touch controller, while Motion can use MotionVFX for color grading, 3D camera tracking, and visual effects. Compressor gains support for encoding videos recorded in Cinematic mode.

Pixelmator Pro includes Generate Fill for images, taking advantage of AI for edits that blend in with surrounding content. Apple says the app can match lighting, perspective, and texture. title: Apple has a handy new menu bar icon in macOS 27.3. Here’s what it does
content:
Macworld





On Monday, Apple released a note to developers covering the updates to Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access in the upcoming macOS 27.3. In addtion to providing a new user interface for configuring FDA, users will notice another new related feature that’s up in the macOS menu bar.
The developer note states that macOS 27.3 will have, “a transparency indicator when a requesting app is controlling another app using System & App Protection Override.” That indicator comes in the form of a blue icon that looks like a stack behind a cursor. When you click on it, a pop-up menu lists the apps with permissions for System & App Protection Override. On X, arinwaichulis posted screenshots of how it looks.


Another interesting detail in macOS 27.3 beta 2 is this new stack icon
If you give any app full disk access it's PERMANENTLY displayed in the menu bar and updates you on everything it's accessed pic.twitter.com/embqGmvTly
— Arin (@arinwaichulis) November 17, 2026





While arinwaichulis states that the feature lists FDA apps, FDA is different from System & App Protection Override, which is a state where an app controls other apps and can bypass system protections. FDA allows apps to read, change, delete, and export data on your Mac. It’s a nuanced difference, but an app could fall in one category and not necessarily the other. Based on what the developer note said, it’s likely that this is a list of apps granted System & App Protection Override permissions.
The indicator appears in the menu bar by default in the macOS 27.3 beta 2. There currently is no way in System Settings to turn it off and have it not appear, but 9to5Mac posted a way to do it through Terminal commands. In Terminal, enter the following (enter your password when prompted):
sudo mkdir -p /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain
sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false
To restore the indicator, use the following Terminal command: sudo defaults delete /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false and restart the Mac.
We’re expecting macOS 27.3 to wrap up beta testing and releae in early to mid-December.

title: The new HomePod mini’s boring colors finally make sense to me
content:
Macworld





Yesterday I made a rare trip south of the Thames to visit Apple’s stunning Battersea Power Station headquarters in London, where I was given a chance to try out HomeView (on which I will soon have more to say) as well as the new Apple TV and HomePod mini. And while I was there, one of the product managers helped me to reach a small logical breakthrough.
I spend far too much time thinking about product colors, and was quite loudly critical when the options for the 2nd-gen HomePod mini were unveiled last month. There are still five finishes, and these still include black, white, and very dark blue. But the two nicest from 2021, a rich autumnal orange and a glorious marigold yellow, both of which I promptly bought, have been replaced by dark green and a washed-out pink. This, in my opinion, is displeasing.

				
					

				
			The somber new color options for 2026.Apple
Photography doesn’t always do justice to the color of tech products, and my first thought when wandering around the demo environment was that the new HomePod mini looks nicer in the flesh than I expected. The pink is still paler than I’d like, but it’s fine, and the green is undeniably smart. Even the ostensibly most boring options, black and white and dark blue, work in a real-world context in a way they don’t on a webpage with a white background.
The real revelation, however, came when the product manager showed me a stereo pair of green HomePods which had been set up either side of a green iMac. The new models, he casually mentioned, were color-matched to the company’s famously attractive all-in-one desktop.
Right. Of course.
Now, it’s important to stress that this doesn’t mean the two sets of products are in every case exactly the same shade (although the greens are remarkably close, as you can see above). Nor does it mean that the two ranges line up perfectly; there’s no black iMac, while the HomePod mini range doesn’t have a purple option, and as previously mentioned no longer includes orange and yellow. Essentially what we mean is that the green, blue, and pink HomePods will go nicely with the green, blue, and pink iMacs.

				
					

				
			The HomePod mini’s color options in 2021. (When it launched in 2020, only black and white were available.)
Apple




The point is that, where colors are offered on both products, they have been explicitly and consciously designed to go together harmoniously. This hasn’t always been the case. The bright orange and yellow HomePods, for example, were not (at least in my subjective view) a good match for the orange and yellow iMacs, because they’re different renditions of those colors. The orange HomePod is insufficiently peachy and the yellow HomePod too orangey to work well with their equivalents. And they’re both too bold to suit the softer colors of the iMac.
In other words, while the new colors may not be quite as exciting as the last set, they’re more considered and a lot more co-ordinated. And on this type of tech, that counts.
When you consider a product purely as an object in isolation or on an otherwise blank page, bright colors seem like the way to go. But when you think decoratively, as we must for home tech, it’s sometimes better to go for a safe color which won’t clash with the carpet or the wallpaper. You have to consider the other elements. And even though I remain a fan of bright colors, Apple’s choice to go for duller options this year now makes a lot more sense to me.

title: New Apple products coming in 2027: What’s next?
content:
Macworld





What new products will Apple launch in 2027? Rumors point to a redesigned iPhone to mark its 20th anniversary, an OLED iPad Air, and potentially Apple’s first smart glasses. Updated Macs, more affordable iPhones and new AI-focused accessories could also be on the way.
The first launches could arrive in the spring. Reports suggest Apple will introduce the standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, potentially alongside an updated iPhone Air. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman also expects new entry-level iPad, iPad Air and iPad Pro models in the first half of 2027.
Later in the year, attention will turn to the iPhone’s anniversary redesign, while camera-equipped AirPods and further smart-home developments could expand Apple’s lineup. 
Below, we round up the latest Apple product rumors for 2027 and beyond, including expected release dates, possible features and whether an upcoming update makes it worth waiting before you buy. Read on to find out what new products to expect at Apple’s next event and in 2027 and beyond.
Apple’s roadmap: At a glance

Every New Apple Product Launching in 2027 and beyond
In the sections below we’ve split the upcoming new products into categories including Mac, iPad, iPhone, Apple Watch, Home, AirPods, and some new product categories.


						

							







What new iPhones are coming in 2027?
Reports point to a split iPhone launch schedule in 2027, with the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e and potentially an updated iPhone Air arriving in spring. A major redesign could follow in the fall to mark the iPhone’s 20th anniversary. There is a lot of speculation about whether Apple will use the iPhone 19 or iPhone 20 name.

				
					

				
			There are new iPhones coming.
Foundry




iPhone 18 & iPhone 18e
Spring 2027 launch expected
The iPhone 18 and 18e are rumored to arrive together in the spring of 2027. Both could gain A20 chips and more RAM. The iPhone 18 is expected to retain dual rear cameras and gain a 24MP selfie camera; the 18e may keep one rear camera and a 60Hz display. Read about the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e rumors. 
iPhone Air 2
First half of 2027 rumored
The iPhone Air could also be getting an update. But there are rumors that it will actually merge with the iPhone 18. See our iPhone Air 2 rumors.
iPhone 19 or 20 – 20th anniversary iPhone 
Apple’s 20th-anniversary iPhone could feature curved glass, ultra-thin bezels and two larger display sizes. Under-display Face ID could reduce the camera cutout. See our iPhone 19 or 20 rumors – because one thing nobody is sure about is whether Apple will skip 19 like it skipped 9 with the arrival of the iPhone X. 
iPhone Duo 2
Apple’s second-generation iPhone Duo could arrive in fall 2027, with Face ID and an Action button among the reported priorities.
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has a prototype with Face ID hardware. More substantial changes, including a telephoto camera and a thinner, lighter design, reportedly remain longer-term goals and not arrive until 2028 or later. 
Should you buy now or wait? 
If you need an iPhone now, compare current models with discounted older stock and refurbished alternatives. If your existing phone still meets your needs and you’re considering a standard or lower-cost model, waiting for the rumored spring 2027 launches may give you more choice. See our guide to When is the best time to buy an iPhone.


						

							


Which new iPads are coming in 2027?
Apple is reportedly planning updates to the entry-level iPad, iPad Air and iPad Pro in the first half of 2027. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the Air could gain an OLED display, while the Pro is expected to offer faster performance and vapor-chamber cooling. 

				
					

				
			
Screenshot

First half of 2027 rumored
When Apple updated the standard iPad in March 2025, the biggest disappointment was its A16 chip, which doesn’t support Apple Intelligence. The next model is expected to address that with an A18 or A19 chip, bringing Apple’s AI features to its entry-level tablet.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman previously predicted a 2026 launch but now expects the new iPad in the first quarter of 2027 at the earliest. Read more in our new iPad rumor roundup.
iPad Air
First half of 2027 rumored
The next iPad Air could gain an OLED display, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. That would make screen quality a potentially significant part of this update, alongside any processor improvements.
iPad Pro
First half of 2027 rumored
Gurman also expects a faster iPad Pro with vapor-chamber cooling. The cooling system could help manage heat during gaming and demanding AI tasks. 
Apple Pencil USB-C and Pro
Apple is reportedly preparing updated versions of both the Apple Pencil USB-C and Apple Pencil Pro for early 2027, potentially alongside new iPads. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has suggested that changes could include batteries that are easier to replace.
Should you buy now or wait? 
With the iPad prices increasing in June 2026, you may want to hold off buying one now. If you are going to pay more at least get the most up-to-date model, or buy from Apple’s Refurbished Store to get a bargain. Read Should I buy an iPad now or wait?


						

							


Which new Macs are coming in 2027?
2026 was a significant year for the Mac, with Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro and a new entry-level laptop – the MacBook Neo. What is in store for 2027?
MacBook Air with M6 
Now that the MacBook Pro, iMac and Mac mini have the M6 chip, it’s only a matter of time before the MacBook Air gets its processor upgrade. 
MacBook Neo 2
Currently, the MacBook Neo is powered by the A18 Pro chip. We expect it will get an upgrade to the A19 Pro or A20 Pro chip.
A larger iMac

				
					

				
			The iMac Pro with its large display and powerful processor is missed. 
Apple




Apple has launched the M6 iMac, but could there be something bigger coming? Reports suggest Apple has explored a new iMac Pro with a 32-inch mini-LED display. Pro-level performance is rumored, with more powerful chips and greater memory capacity than the standard model.
Read about the larger iMac rumors.
Should you buy now or wait? 
With the prices of Macs increasing in June due to the global RAM shortages you may want to hold off buying one now. If you are going to pay more at least get the most up-to-date model, or buy from Apple’s Refurbished Store to get a bargain. Read the following for more guidance:
Should you buy the MacBook Pro now or wait? 
Should you buy the MacBook Air now or wait?
Should you buy a Mac mini now or wait?
Should you buy a Mac Studio now or wait?


						

							


New Apple Watches coming in 2027
So far we only have a limited picture of Apple Watch plans for 2027: no specific 2027 models or confirmed features are identified. 

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




Apple Watch Series 13
The Apple Watch Series 13 could get a redesign in what is rumored to be one of the biggest Apple Watch upgrades in years. As well as a new design, a new way to attach bands, and a better display, we could see improved health sensors. 
Apple Watch SE 4
With no new Apple Watch in 2026, an update in 2027 seems likely based on Apple’s historical two-to-three-year upgrade cycle. 


						

							


New AirPods coming in 2027

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods with a camera?
According to a brief update in Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter for Bloomberg in August, Apple is aiming to launch camera-equipped AirPods.
The new earbuds are expected to resemble the AirPods Pro 3, although it’s not yet clear whether they will also include a heart rate sensor.
The cameras are said to include both visible-light and infrared sensors, but they reportedly won’t be designed for taking photos or recording video, as their placement and image quality would make them unsuitable for those tasks. Instead, the cameras are expected to enable AI-powered features, such as hand gesture recognition, adapting audio based on the surrounding environment, and detecting whether someone is speaking directly to you or simply talking nearby.
Wondering whether to buy AirPods? Read Should I buy AirPods now and our AirPods buying guide. 


						

							


Software updates
Apple released iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 and its other major updates in September 2026, introducing Siri AI, expanded Apple Intelligence features, new parental controls and app improvements. Further point updates will bring additional features, refinements and bug fixes.
For current features, availability and forthcoming additions, see our macOS 27 and iOS 27 guides. Our separate  latest iOS beta and latest macOS beta guides track testing of future updates.
Siri and Apple Intelligence
Siri AI brings more natural conversations, personal-context and onscreen awareness, and more actions across apps. Not every promised Siri AI feature was available at launch. 
October’s 27.2 updates added French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish alongside English. Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish and Vietnamese are due by year-end. In the EU, Siri AI is available on macOS but remains unavailable on iOS, iPadOS and watchOS.
Availability depends on device, language and region, and some users may need to join a waiting list.
iOS 28, iPadOS 28, macOS 28
Apple is expected to preview its next major operating systems at WWDC in June 2027, followed by summer beta testing and public releases in the fall.


						

							


Apple smart-home products coming in 2027 and beyond
In October 2026 Apple announced a major expansion of its smart-home lineup with the launch of the HomeView, HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K and the Apple Home Collection at its “Welcome Home” experience. We are still waiting for the update to the larger HomePod, with hope that could arrive in 2027.

				
					

				
			
Screenshot

Foundry




HomePod 3
Expected: 2027 
The HomePod mini was updated in 2026, but not the larger HomePod. The reason for the delay may be that a more advanced HomePod speaker featuring a built-in display is coming. 
HomeView Ultra
Possible release: Late 2027 at the earliest, potentially 2028, according to The Information.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is developing a higher-end HomeView, codenamed J595, with a 9-inch display mounted on a motorized arm. The screen could rotate through 360 degrees and automatically turn toward whoever is speaking.
A November 2 report from The Information suggests the device could cost around $1,000 and arrive in late 2027 at the earliest, although its launch could slip into 2028. Development of its autonomous AI features reportedly remains a constraint, with Apple still deciding which capabilities to include in the first-generation model. Cameras and sensors could allow it to respond to its surroundings – for example, turning on lights when someone enters a room.
This would be a separate, more advanced model than the 7-inch HomeView announced in October 2026. Apple has not announced the device, and “HomeView Max” and “HomeView Ultra” remain speculative names. Read more about the HomeView Ultra here: ‘HomeView Ultra’ with robot arm may be coming next year


						

							


Upcoming Vision devices, AR and spatial computing
Apple Smart Glasses 
Possible June 2027 launch, shipping by end of 2027
Apple could unveil its first smart glasses at WWDC in June 2027, with shipments following before the end of the year, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. However, software development is reportedly running behind, so delays remain possible.
The first-generation glasses are expected to combine cameras, speakers and Siri-powered features, including Visual Intelligence and voice-controlled actions in apps. They reportedly won’t have a display for overlaying digital information on the wearer’s surroundings. Multiple frame styles and colors are also being developed.
Vision Pro
Possible 2028 update
Prior to 2026, Apple’s spatial computing strategy has focused on the high-end market, but reports indicate a more affordable version of the headset is in development. Apple has reportedly paused work on a successor to the high-end Vision Pro and could instead release a cheaper Vision Pro.

title: iPhone Duo 2 Likely to Retain Touch ID as Face ID Remains Uncertain
content:
Apple's second-generation iPhone Duo will retain its existing display sizes and side-mounted fingerprint sensor, according to the leaker known as "Digital Chat Station."


In a new post on Weibo, the leaker said information about the ‌iPhone Duo‌ 2 remains limited, but engineering units continue to feature a 7.6-inch inner display, a 5.4-inch outer display, and a fingerprint sensor on the side, with no clear sign of Face ID being added to the device. Those details carry over the screen sizes and Touch ID arrangement of the first-generation model.

Digital Chat Station also questioned ‌Face ID‌'s space requirements and practicality if limited to the outer display, which faces away from the user when unfolded. Users might need to switch to ‌Touch ID‌ when using the inner screen, or turn the device around to authenticate with ‌Face ID‌, creating what the leaker suggested would be a disjointed experience.

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said on Sunday that Apple has developed ‌iPhone Duo‌ 2 prototypes with ‌Face ID‌ on the outer display, but is running out of time to finalize the feature, meaning it could slip to the third generation.

Face Unlock option for the existing ‌iPhone Duo‌ in iOS 27.3 beta 2. Called "Unlock with Front Camera," the feature uses the standard outer camera to unlock the device when closed. It does not provide the depth-sensing authentication of ‌Face ID‌, cannot authorize Apple Pay purchases or autofill passwords, and still requires ‌Touch ID‌ or a passcode when the device is unfolded.

20th anniversary models, including displays that curve around all four edges. The second-generation ‌iPhone Duo‌ is expected to launch in the fall of 2027.

WhatsApp cloud backup options in iOS beta (image: WABetaInfo)

The option is said to be appearing to some users on WhatsApp beta version 26.45.10.71, currently in TestFlight, providing users with an alternative to iCloud chat backup for the first time.

July that suggested users would eventually be able to pick their preferred backup destination directly from the app's chat backup settings. iCloud remains the default, but the WhatsApp backup option differs in that it is fully end-to-end encrypted, and dedicated to chat backups only.

title: Best iPhone Duo cases: Slim, protective and kickstand options
content:
Macworld





Apple’s new iPhone Duo is both big and small, and it’s more susceptible to knocks and drops than a standard iPhone with its folding function maybe taking a while to get used to. It’s the first iPhone that needs a case built around moving parts—namely the hinge. A case for a foldable can be made from one or two shells, with the additional question of covering the hinge or leaving it bare. The phone goes on sale October 23, and cases are already arriving.
iPhone Duo test criteria
We look for eight key criteria when testing each case.

				
					

				
			Our test surrogate Duo in the Benks ArmorGrid Air (Beyond Blue)
Simon Jary




Protection: We checked corner reinforcement, camera and screen-edge protection, hinge coverage, and how much of the handset each shell covers. We did not run our own drop tests, so protection assessments are based on construction and coverage, and we note manufacturer claims as claims. Some case makers specify the exact measurements of their raised screen and camera edges, other do not. 
Materials and grip: We assess surface texture, grip, finish, and visible fingerprint marks during handling. Common case materials include TPU (thermoplastic polyurethane, a flexible, durable plastic) and aramid fiber (a lightweight, high-strength synthetic fiber, best known through the Kevlar brand). The material alone does not establish how well a case protects the phone; construction and coverage also matter. Long-term wear, discoloration, and adhesive durability cannot be established during these initial checks.
Hinge protection and operation: Cases take different approaches to the Duo’s hinge: some include a protective cover, while others leave it exposed. We opened and closed each case on the dummy handset, checking for stiffness, rattling, gaps, and smooth movement of any hinge cover. We also checked whether both shells stayed firmly attached during opening and closing. These checks provide an initial assessment of the case’s construction and movement. We will assess the effect on the actual phone’s hinge movement or opening angle will require further testing with a working iPhone Duo. 
Fit and installation: We used the dummy iPhone Duo to assess how securely each section fits the handset, the alignment of cutouts, and the ease of installation. We also checked the positioning and accessibility of button covers and port openings. Final fit and tolerances, button response, Touch ID operation, and cable fit will need confirmation with a retail iPhone Duo.
Slimness: The Duo’s thin profile is part of its appeal but this must be weighed against the backplate’s coverage and reinforcement. We penalize cases that add bulk without a clear benefit, but not where the protective benefits are worthwhile.
Extra functions: Some iPhone Duo cases include a kickstand for easier viewing. We assessed adjustability and how much bulk the stand adds. ESR’s Flex Stand, for example, rotates 180° and forms a protective guard around the camera bar when not in use. Other stands, such as those on the Torras Ostand and UAG Mouve XTE, rotate 360° and fold flat against the case backplate. The Moft Dynamic Folio uses an origami-like folding stand. Stability with a working iPhone Duo, both folded and unfolded, will require further testing because its weight and balance may differ from those of the dummy handset.
Colors and style: We assessed the range of colors and the quality of the finishes provided. Most of the color and pattern will be seen on the case’s backplate, but it should also be noticed on the front frame and hinge protector where present.
Magnetic accessory compatibility: We checked how securely magnetic chargers, power banks, wallets, and other accessories attached, and whether the case’s camera surround, hinge protection, or kickstand obstructed their fit. Because we used a dummy handset for our initial testing, these checks assess attachment and clearance only. We will test charging performance—including speed, heat, and reliability—once we have a working iPhone Duo.

There are two Apple-branded cases for the iPhone Duo. The basic version is called simply the Apple iPhone Duo Case. If you want everything to have an Apple logo on it, this is a solid choice you can’t go wrong with.
It’s a two-part design, with each side having its own thin cover and a protective frame around the edges. This leaves the phone’s hinge area “unobstructed” (which the pessimistic among us could also describe as “exposed”) so the device can fold and close completely flat without interference. Like most two-part cases without a hinge cover, it requires adhesive strips to ensure a secure fit, and so is not as easy to remove and reattach as magnetic cases such as Apple’s own Duo Folio case.
Made from polycarbonate with a matte coating, the case is available in two colors—Navy Blue and Sand—that match the Duo’s own Night Sky and Star White colors.

While it does protect the exterior display and the hinge, unlike the basic Apple Duo Case it doesn’t feature a protective frame for the phone’s edges. Somewhat remarkably, the MagSafe connection remains even when the stand cover is closed and will also work when it’s open. The Duo can wirelessly charge at up to 25W.
Again, the Navy Blue and Taupe case colors are suited to each of the two Duo appearances. It’s made with Apple’s leather-alternative TechWoven fabric, found on its standard iPhone cases. The whole package weighs a slight 23.5g in Beyond Blue (shown here); strangely the Obsidian Black version weighs less at just 18.8g and is marginally thinner at 1.2mm vs 1.3mm. You won’t notice the difference.
There’s no hinge protection, which keeps the Duo’s folding mechanism unencumbered and reduces the possible points of failure but also leaves this area of the Duo bare. Benks includes replacement adhesive strips in case you frequently remove the front frame.

FAQ
Does the iPhone Duo need a case?
No phone needs a protective case until you drop or knock it. A case isn’t essential for the iPhone Duo, but it’s a sensible investment for a $1,999 foldable. Apple’s Ceramic Shield glass helps protect the displays, but the titanium edges and hinge remain vulnerable to accidental drops, scratches and dents. Unlike conventional iPhone cases, Duo designs must accommodate two halves and a slim cover-screen frame, often using adhesive to stay securely attached.
What to consider when choosing an iPhone Duo case?
Prioritize a precise fit, shock-absorbing corners and the level of coverage you think you need. Raised lips help protect the exterior display and camera, while a dedicated hinge guard covers the folding spine. Check that the case allows easy access to Touch ID and Camera Control without obstructing the inner display or folding mechanism. Since the Duo already weighs 8.9oz (254g), consider whether extra bulk from a kickstand or hinge protector is worthwhile. Choose a slim two-piece case for everyday protection or a hinge-cover design for additional coverage.
Will a case interfere with the iPhone Duo’s hinge or folding action?
A properly fitted iPhone Duo case shouldn’t interfere with folding, but poorly designed hinge covers can add bulk or restrict movement. Some two-piece cases leave the hinge exposed; others include a separate hinge cover, while dedicated covers provide an additional barrier against knocks and grit. However, hinge coverage doesn’t necessarily mean dust protection. Debris can collect between the case and phone, so remove the case periodically and gently clean both surfaces according to Apple’s care guidance. For cases secured with adhesive strips, follow the manufacturer’s removal and cleaning instructions, and check whether replacement strips are required before refitting.
Can I remove and reuse an iPhone Duo case?
That depends on how the case attaches. Some iPhone Duo cases use adhesive strips to secure the front frame or other components. Don’t assume those strips will retain their grip after removal: check whether the manufacturer allows reuse, supplies spare strips, or sells replacements.
A removable component isn’t necessarily reusable with the same adhesive. Before taking off an adhesive-mounted case for cleaning or swapping cases, follow its removal instructions and check what you’ll need to refit it securely.
Is a kickstand case necessary for the iPhone Duo?
If you regularly watch videos, make FaceTime calls or use your iPhone Duo for work, a kickstand case is a useful upgrade. It props up the larger inner display for hands-free viewing, video calls, recipes, and reading. Paired with a Bluetooth keyboard, it can also support light productivity. Some stands double as finger grips for safer handling. The main drawback is added thickness and weight, so look for a stable, well-integrated design that folds flat to the backplate or doubles as a camera bar.
Will MagSafe chargers, wallets, and power banks fit with these cases?
MagSafe uses magnets to align and attach compatible wireless chargers, power banks, wallets, and other accessories. The cases listed here are described as MagSafe compatible, but that doesn’t guarantee every accessory will fit.
Because the iPhone Duo is shorter than a conventional iPhone, larger magnetic wireless power banks and wallets may extend beyond its edges or overlap the camera bar. A case’s kickstand or hinge cover may also prevent an accessory from sitting flat or interfere with unfolding the phone.
Before buying, check the accessory’s dimensions and the case maker’s compatibility guidance. With the accessory attached, make sure it clears the cameras and allows the Duo to open fully. Some wallets and power banks may need to be removed before unfolding.
Our initial case assessments used a dummy handset, allowing us to assess physical clearance and attachment, but not wireless charging performance. We’ll add charging results and recommendations for specific accessories after testing them on a working iPhone Duo.
Would I do better getting AppleCare+ instead of a case?
A combination of slim case and AppleCare+ can offer a good balance between preserving the Duo’s design and protecting against costly accidents. A case helps prevent everyday scratches and knocks, while AppleCare+ covers eligible damage under the plan’s terms, subject to service fees. Theft and loss protection may also be available with a suitable plan. Check Apple’s current pricing and conditions before buying. For maximum peace of mind, use both: prevention for everyday mishaps and coverage for expensive repairs.

title: Phishing scams get a new watchdog as Moonlock expands to iPhone
content:

Moonlock on iPhone
The iPhone app centers on Scam Detect, which analyzes content that users paste, scan or share with Moonlock. Rather than flagging something as suspicious, it explains what might be wrong, including links that don't match the sender they're supposed to represent.
Users can send content to Moonlock directly from other apps through the iOS share sheet. The QR code scanner also lets them inspect a destination before opening it, which could help with scams that hide fraudulent websites behind seemingly ordinary codes.
Moonlock's Safe SMS feature takes a more automatic approach. When enabled in iPhone Settings, it filters suspected scam messages from unknown senders into the Junk folder in Messages and explains why each message was flagged.

title: MacPaw's Moonlock Cybersecurity App Launches for iPhone
content:
MacPaw today launched its Moonlock cybersecurity app for the iPhone, bringing the company's consumer-focused security features to mobile for the first time.


Moonlock is designed to help iPhone users recognize and avoid phishing scams and other online threats, according to the company. For example, one of its key features is Scam Detect, which can check suspicious messages and their contents – like screenshots, links, and QR codes – for signs of phishing. 

Users just paste, scan, or share the content directly with Scam Detect, and the Moonlock app will analyze it and provide an assessment explaining why it may be suspicious.

Moonlock includes a number of other security features specific to the iPhone. Safe SMS is an opt-in feature that automatically filters out scam texts, with a record of what was caught and why. Meanwhile, Security Score provides a score from 0 to 100 that reflects the iPhone's security setup, and gives users recommendations on how they can improve it.

With Email Breach History, users can check whether their email address has turned up in a data breach. If so, the feature can reveal the source of the breach, when and what was exposed, and then walk the user through the steps required to secure each affected account.

Moonlock also includes a number of device and network checks, and the app aims to help users review things like their Wi-Fi security, passcode protection, iOS updates, and more, with checklists of recommended one-time actions and step-by-step instructions.

"When we launched Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next," said Oleg Stukalenko, head of product management at Moonlock by MacPaw.
Moonlock is available to download from the App Store or via Setapp, MacPaw's third-party app marketplace. 

Moonlock is offered based on a customizable monthly plan with different rates depending on the number of devices covered. For example, a single-device plan costs $13.50 per month, with yearly billing working out at $4.50 per month. Each plan also has a one-time purchase option. With a Setapp subscription, Moonlock is included for both Mac and iPhone, so no separate iPhone purchase or additional account is required.

title: Apple Reportedly Developing Two Designs for 20th Anniversary iPhone
content:
Apple is currently developing four models with two different designs for the iPhone's 20th anniversary, according to the leaker known as "Ice Universe."


In a new post on Weibo, the leaker outlined the two designs. Two are said to feature flat glass covers and two have glass that curves along all four edges.

One plausible explanation for this is that Apple is developing two sizes (Pro and Pro Max models) with alternative designs, potentially retaining the flatter versions as fallbacks for the more ambitious curved design, rather than planning to launch four models. Another explanation is that the models with flat front glass are standard "iPhone 20" models set to launch after the iPhone 20 Pro.

The curved versions reportedly have bezels measuring around 1mm, but the shape of the surrounding glass makes them almost invisible when viewed head-on, creating an almost borderless appearance. Ice Universe suggested the effect would be particularly striking in person.

Apple has apparently been prototyping the four-sided curved glass design for three years, making several revisions during that time. The design choice is said to remain under consideration, with the earliest versions featuring substantially more pronounced curves that were later reduced.

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman's report from August, which said that Apple had scrapped an earlier, more ambitious anniversary design that used even more glass in place of metal. Gurman said the design planned for 2027 still features curved front and rear glass separated by a thin metal band. Both reports suggest Apple has moderated elements of its original design.

Screen protector samples circulating online show rounded edges with curves along all four sides and very narrow display borders. According to Ice Universe, the screen protectors seen in recent days reflects an early version with greater curvature.

the same glass material as the iPhone Air, but with greater curvature along all four sides. An accompanying illustration depicted rounded front and rear glass meeting a narrow, polished metal frame.

Ice Universe added that industry sources are enthusiastic about the curved glass design, with some expressing greater anticipation for the anniversary model than for a foldable iPhone.

Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected to launch in the fall of 2027. While leakers have referred to the devices as the "iPhone 20 Pro," Apple's naming plans remain unclear.
