title: Apple Rolls Out All-New Maps Experience Across India
content:
Apple today announced the rollout of an all-new Apple Maps experience in India, bringing the company's redesigned map to the country for the first time. The update offers faster and more accurate navigation, more detailed views of roads, buildings, parks, and shopping centers, and over 300 three-dimensional landmarks.


Notably, the new enhanced map includes features built specifically for India. For example, Natural Language Guidance, which gives directions in conversational phrases such as "At the next traffic light, turn left," has been enhanced with real-world details like pillars and other points of interest. The idea is for Maps to be able to guide users along roads that have no names with directions like "Turn right after the petrol pump." 

Elsewhere, dual-language labels show place names in both English and the local language of a region, just like the country's road signs. Alongside English and Hindi, Apple Maps has added support for Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Punjabi, Odia, and Urdu.

The rollout also brings Look Around to India for the first time, giving users anywhere in the world interactive street-level imagery with high-resolution 3D photography. It also adds AR Walking Directions, which overlay step-by-step guidance onto the real world when users raise their iPhone.

Other features now available in India include lane guidance, multi-stop routing for up to 15 stops with routes that sync from Mac and iPad to iPhone, Share ETA, cycling directions with elevation details, and electric vehicle routing that can plan trips around charging stops. Users can also report accidents, hazards, and speed checks hands-free by telling Siri AI. 

Lastly, transit riders in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, and Pune (as well as on Indian Railways) can use Apple Maps to plan journeys, find nearby stations, and get notifications when it's time to get off at their stop.
"Apple Maps is the best way to explore and navigate the world, and we are excited to bring an enhanced Maps experience to even more users with today's rollout of the new map in India," said Max Muller, Apple's VP of Apple Maps. "The new map offers some of our users' favourite features like Look Around and AR Walking Directions, but we've also designed the map for India's specific navigation needs, including enhanced Natural Language Guidance and customized dual-language labels, making it easier than ever for users to find the places they love and get to where they're going."
The redesigned Apple Maps first launched in the United States in 2018 and has expanded to more countries in the years since, but India has remained a notable gap, despite Apple opening a Maps-focused development center in Hyderabad back in 2016. Turn-by-turn navigation only arrived in the country in 2019.

title: Your iPhone’s USB-C port can do a lot more than fast-charge
content:
Macworld





The iPhone 15 and later have a USB-C port that can do more than charge your phone. You can plug in an external SSD, import photos from an SD card, connect wired headphones, or top up your AirPods or Apple Watch. Most USB-C iPhones can also connect to a monitor or TV. Here’s what works with your iPhone and which cables or adapters you’ll need.
Which iPhones have USB-C?
Apple switched from Lightning to USB-C with the iPhone 15 lineup in 2023. Every iPhone released since then has USB-C, but file transfer speeds and support for wired monitors and TVs vary by model.


iPhone modelsMaximum USB data speedWired monitor or TV support

iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max, 16 Pro and Pro Max
17 Pro and Pro Max, 18 Pro and Pro Max, and iPhone DuoUSB 3, up to 10GbpsYes
iPhone 15 and 15 Plus, iPhone 16 and 16 Plus, and iPhone 17USB 2, up to 480MbpsYes
iPhone 16e, iPhone 17e, and iPhone AirUSB 2, up to 480MbpsNo

 



The USB-C cable that comes with your iPhone supports charging and data transfers at up to 480Mbps. To get up to 10Gbps when copying files to an external SSD or computer, you’ll need a compatible iPhone from the first row, a USB-C cable rated for 10Gbps, and a drive or computer port that supports that speed. 


1. Charge AirPods or an Apple Watch from your iPhone
Rival companies like Samsung have long supported reverse wireless charging, letting you turn your smartphone into a portable Qi charging pad. That usually means flipping your phone over and leaving it face down while the other device charges. With the iPhone 15, Apple introduced its own take on reverse charging using the USB-C port.
Your iPhone can deliver up to 4.5W of power, enough to top up your AirPods, Apple Watch, or even a friend’s compatible Android phone when you’re away from an outlet. For AirPods, grab a USB-C-to-USB-C or USB-C-to-Lightning cable, depending on the port on your charging case. To charge an Apple Watch, plug its USB-C magnetic charging cable into your iPhone and place the watch on the puck.


						

							


2. Connect an external SSD or USB flash drive
Most of us have seen the iPhone’s storage-full alert. If you’d rather keep a local copy of your files than rely on iCloud, you can plug an external SSD or USB flash drive into your iPhone’s USB-C port. It’s an easy way to move large files off your phone and free up space.
Connect the drive.
Open the Files app.
Tap Browse.
Select the drive under Locations. 
Now you can open files on the drive or copy them to and from your iPhone. 
A compact Samsung Type-C Flash Drive ($80) is a handy option for everyday transfers. If you’re using a drive that needs more power than the iPhone can supply, connect it through a powered USB hub.
If you shoot ProRes video on an iPhone 15 Pro through iPhone 18 Pro, including the Pro Max models, you can record directly to a compatible external SSD. ProRes files take up a lot of space, so recording to a drive can help you shoot longer without filling up your iPhone. For 4K at 60 fps, use an exFAT-formatted SSD that can sustain write speeds of at least 220 MB/s and a 10Gbps USB-C data cable.

				
					

				
			
Your iPhone’s USB-C cable can do more than just charge your iPhone.

Foundry



							


3. Import photos and videos from an SD card
Photographers and videographers love the handy SD card slots on the MacBook Pro and Mac Studio, and a wired SD card reader brings that same convenience to your iPhone. While many newer cameras support wireless photo transfers through their companion apps, plugging in the card can be quicker when you have a lot of photos or videos to import.
Plug a reader such as Apple’s USB-C to SD Card Reader  ($39) into your iPhone’s charging port and insert the card from your camera. Open Photos, tap Import, then choose Import All or select the photos and videos you want to copy. To browse the card’s folders or copy other files, open Files, tap Browse, and select the card under Locations.
You can also use the same reader with a USB-C Mac or iPad when you want to edit on a larger screen. See our roundup of the best USB-C adapters.


						

							


4. Connect your iPhone to a monitor or TV
If you’re staying at a hotel that blocks wireless casting, you may still be able to mirror your iPhone’s screen by plugging it into the TV. First, check your model. The iPhone 16e, iPhone 17e, and iPhone Air lack wired video output over USB-C. With those models, you can use AirPlay if the hotel TV supports it, or stream to an Apple TV. 
If your iPhone supports wired video and the TV has an accessible HDMI port, use a USB-C-to-HDMI cable or plug Apple’s USB-C Digital AV Multiport Adapter ($69) into your iPhone and connect it to the TV with a separate HDMI cable. Switch the TV to that HDMI input. With a compatible TV, Apple’s adapter supports up to 4K at 60Hz. 
If your monitor has a USB-C video input, you can plug your iPhone directly into it using the cable that came with the monitor or another USB-C cable that supports DisplayPort video. Unfortunately, the charging cable included with your iPhone won’t work for this.
Check out our roundups of the best monitors and best portable monitors.

				
					

				
			
Your iPhone can connect to most displays with a single cable.

Foundry



							


5. Connect your iPhone to wired CarPlay
Apple introduced wireless CarPlay a few years ago, but if your car only supports wired CarPlay, you’ll still need to plug your iPhone into the car’s USB port. Look for a CarPlay or smartphone icon beside the port, then use a USB-C-to-USB-A cable if it’s a rectangular USB-A port, or a USB-C-to-USB-C cable if it’s USB-C. Make sure the cable supports both data and charging, is long enough to reach the port, and is flexible enough to route around any knobs or vents.
A coiled cable can help keep the extra length out of the way. These popular Chubby Cable car-charging cables come in USB-C-to-USB-C and USB-C-to-USB-A versions for $20, with a variety of colors to choose from. If your iPhone charges but CarPlay doesn’t appear, check that you’re plugged into the port designated for CarPlay and try a different cable that supports data.
Read further: Best magnetic wireless and USB car chargers and mounts for iPhone.


						

							


6. Connect a keyboard
While iPads and Macs are better suited for long-form typing, iPhones—especially the near-7-inch Plus and Pro Max models—can still handle productivity tasks effectively. To make the most of the relatively small screen, though, you may want to pair it with a dedicated keyboard. Fortunately, iOS natively supports this through the USB-C port.
Most standard keyboards, such as this compact Macally keyboard ($30), will work with your iPhone just fine. See our roundup of the best Mac keyboards. Or if you want to always have a keyboard with you, you can opt for a Clicks case ($139), which connects to your USB-C port so it’s always ready for a text or email. 


						

							


7. Amplify your microphone
In the era of TikTok, everyone is a content creator, so a high-quality microphone is an essential tool. Fortunately, your iPhone’s USB-C port can support a wide range of them, letting you pair your footage with crystal-clear high-quality audio. One reliable option is the Rode Wireless Micro ($85), which utilizes your iPhone’s port while maintaining the convenience of wireless recording.


						

							


8. Plug in a game controller
Thanks to the A17 and A18 chips, the latest Pro-tier iPhones can run some AAA games. Notably, though, these titles typically need a controller, as touch controls don’t always offer the best gameplay, if they’re available at all. While Sony’s DualSense controller ($75) supports Bluetooth pairing, opting for wired mode using the iPhone’s USB-C port can minimize latency and enhance overall performance.


						

							


9. Connect to Ethernet 
Speaking of gaming, the iPhone fully supports Ethernet dongles, allowing for faster download and upload speeds. While Wi-Fi and 5G are sufficient for most users, Ethernet can come in handy when seeking an even more dependable connection. Belkin’s USB-C to Ethernet Adapter ($23) is one of the solid options that is guaranteed to get the job done.


						

							


10. Peer into small places
There are many accessories that you can plug into your iPhone’s USB-C port, but none are cooler than a borescope/endoscope camera. Basically, it’s a snake wire with a tiny HD endoscope camera at the end and an LCD light. It’s flexible yet rigid enough to fit into the smallest of crevices, and you’ll wonder how you ever lived without it. We haven’t tested them, but this model has a 4.3-star rating with nearly 7,000 reviews and costs just $30.

				
					

				
			
You can attach a tiny USB-C camera to your iPhone’s USB-C port to see into small places.

Amazon



							


11. Cool off in summer
With temperatures steadily rising all around the world, we can all use a little relief during long days outdoors. Your iPhone’s USB-C port can help there too. This 17,000 RPM ,4-setting high-speed fan ($15) plugs directly into your iPhone’s USB-C port and offers a “focused airflow channel that generates a high-speed airflow of up to 36 ft/s.” Reviewers praise its size, portability, and low-power requirements, but you’ll just appreciate a quick blast of cool air when you’re overheating.


						

							


12. Plug and don’t play
When you’re not using your iPhone’s USB-C port, it’s just a gaping hole at the bottom of your phone waiting to collect dust, dirt, and lint. A USB-C plug will make sure your port stays clean and clear for as long as you use your iPhone. You can get a bunch of them ($7) for just a few bucks, or you can get one that sticks to the back of your phone ($8), so you don’t keep losing them. An added bonus: it doubles as a handy pinky rest when you’re using your iPhone with one hand.
Read further: How to stop dust, dirt, and lint from getting into your iPhone charging port.


						

							


One port can do it all
The biggest detriment of the iPhone is that there’s just one port, but a USB hub can give you much more. We recommend the Plugable 7-in-1 USB-C Hub Multiport Adapter ($40), which will bring a headphone jack, USB-C charging, HDMI, an SD card reader, Ethernet, and even a couple of USB-A ports for good measure. It’s not exactly small, but if you need to use several ports at once, there’s no substitute.

				
					

				
			
Your iPhone’s USB-C port is a multi-purpose connector for displays, hard drives, and other accessories.

Connor Jewiss / Foundry




Michael Simon contributed to this report.

title: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 Display Production to Begin Soon Ahead of Expected March Launch
content:
Apple's display suppliers are preparing to begin mass production of OLED panels for the upcoming iPhone Air 2 and iPhone 18, according to a report from Korea's ETNews.


The devices will mark Apple's first spring releases next year as part of the company's new split-launch strategy for its flagship smartphones. Apple already debuted the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo in September. The iPhone 18e, Apple's more affordable option, is also expected to launch in the spring.

The report claims Samsung Display and LG Display appear to be aligning their production plans for an expected March 2027 launch schedule. The two companies are expected to start mass production in late December and early January, with Samsung said to be the sole supplier for the iPhone Air 2. Apple is also said to have existing OLED panel inventory that it can use for the Air 2.

improved shipment times edge into December from the original January 2027 forecast. 

The standard iPhone and Air models typically account for more than 30% of total iPhone lineup sales, with the standard model outselling the Air, according to the report.

As for upgrades, the iPhone 18 is rumored to get an A20 chip built on Apple's 2nm process, either 9GB or 12GB of RAM depending on the rumor source, a smaller Dynamic Island, and Apple's C2 modem. 

The iPhone Air 2 is expected to gain a second rear camera, with an Ultra Wide lens in addition to the Wide lens. Apple is also likely to increase the battery life of the ultra-slim device, reduce the size of the Dynamic Island, and adopt Apple's 2nm A20 chip for speed and efficiency improvements. The Air 2 is also likely to get the C2 modem.

title: The best Apple upgrade this season won’t cost you a penny
content:
Macworld





It’s been a loaded fall for Apple fans. Over the past couple of months, the company launched around a dozen new products, including several brand-new products rumored for years. Many have been sold out for weeks and months, and millions of people are still basking in the new-device glow of the iPhone Duo, PROLED MacBook Pro, and HomeView.
Even so, there are enough issues with the new devices, not to mention high prices, to convince many users to stick with their existing setups for another year. Apple hasn’t forgotten you. In just a few weeks, iOS 27.3 and the rest of the OS updates will bring a fresh wave of useful additions to older devices. So even if you’re skipping the hardware upgrades this season, your iPhone, iPad, and Mac are getting a bunch of excellent new features before the year is up.
The good dark web
Seven years ago, Apple brought system-wide dark mode to the iPhone with iOS 13. While most popular apps have implemented support for the theme, many websites remain restricted to the light look, contributing to eye strain when browsing at night. Safari on iOS 27.3—as well as iPadOS and macOS—remedies the situation by implementing an Adaptive Dark Mode toggle.
When enabled, the feature automatically adapts bright webpages to dark mode by tweaking the colors of the background, text, and other assets. The perk is completely optional, and you can exclude individual websites if you so prefer. While this can effectively replace dedicated Safari extensions that serve the same purpose, third-party tools will remain relevant for some power users. After all, Apple’s implementation isn’t personalizable and doesn’t provide the same level of control. It just works.
Other Safari additions offered by iOS 27.3 beta include a vertical tab layout solely on the iPhone Duo. (If you haven’t bought a Duo, worry not, as iPadOS and macOS 27.3 beta bring the same feature to your existing devices.) This stacks open Safari tabs vertically along the side, as opposed to the traditional horizontal row.
And speaking of macOS, this beta release also ports the Now Playing Live Activity’s colorful waveform on the touchscreen MacBook Pro to all other Macs. While the Dynamic Island itself remains a high-end exclusive, older Macs won’t miss out on the experience anymore.

				
					

				
			
Safari has a new Adaptive Dark Mode to force websites to darken light websites.

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry




Functional gains
For years, Apple Fitness+ has offered hundreds of guided workout videos and meditation sessions, helping subscribers stay active. With watchOS 27.3 beta, the paid service adds a new Gym Strength feature that can build a custom workout plan based on your available equipment, schedule, and readiness. Once the plan is set up, you simply follow the selected trainer’s instructions, and you get to adjust the load and rep counts if the defaults don’t match your level. To use Gym Strength, your iPhone or iPad must also be running the OS 27.3 beta—not just your Apple Watch.
Karaoke camera
Apple Music is another subscription service getting some love with iOS 27.3 beta. After updating your iPhone, a new Selfie Sing button will appear when viewing the lyrics of compatible songs. The feature upgrades the existing karaoke experience by letting you record a short video of yourself with an overlay of the track’s title, cover, and real-time lyrics. 
It’s a fun perk that makes sharing music with friends or on social media more engaging and personal, but the supported catalog appears to be very limited for now. To spare you from hunting, Apple has compiled some of the eligible songs in a dedicated playlist.

				
					

				
			
Standby mode gets an upgrade in iOS 27.3

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry




Déjà Duo
With the iPhone Duo launch, Apple introduced a revamped StandBy mode that works exclusively on its foldable without needing a charger. The redesigned experience unlocks support for more advanced color and layout customizations, similar to those available with Apple Watch faces. Thankfully, iOS 27.3 beta brings some of these options to regular iPhones—although charging is still required. After installing the update, tap and hold on the screen in StandBy mode to add, edit, or delete a custom look.
Speaking of the iPhone Duo, the second beta of iOS 27.3 also introduces the ability to unlock the phone with the front camera when it’s closed as long as Touch ID has been used within 45 minutes.
Agentic age
iOS 27.3 beta boosts Siri AI’s agentic capabilities by letting it execute complex in-app tasks using voice or text commands. The upgraded functionality is already live in most of Apple’s built-in applications, including Mail, Messages, Calendar, Safari, Files, and Reminders. Managing Safari tabs, organizing files, and scheduling iMessages are some of the handy actions you can try right away. If you’re not sure where to start, you can launch the desired app and ask Siri what it can do.
With this OS release, Apple also enables third-party developers to adopt similar advancements in their apps using the App Intents framework. And with the new Siri AI skills, developers can teach the assistant to merge multiple actions into one. This should simplify controlling apps in a hands-free manner.

				
					

				
			
The redesigned Health app looks to finally arrive on iPhones with iOS 27.3.

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry




Healthy facelift
Lastly, iOS 27.3 beta brings back the overhauled Health app that Apple briefly tested during the iOS 27.2 beta cycle. The new interface surfaces relevant health and fitness data in a more visually appealing way and introduces all-new insights like Health Age and AI-powered tips.
iOS 27.3 is currently available to developers and public beta testers. If you are familiar with the associated risks—which include the potential of bricking your device and losing local data—and would like to try the new features today, you can enroll in either beta program and download the available prerelease builds on any of your compatible Apple devices. But it won’t be long before all of these updates arrive for everyone; we’re expecting the final versions to launch around mid-December.

 FAQ 


1.
How much time does Apple Watch take to fast charge? 
The Apple Watch battery life is notoriously short between charges so fast charging is a great way to keep your smart timepiece topped up and ready for action. 
Using a Fast Charger cable, you’ll get fully powered up in the shortest time so look for Watch chargers that support fast-charging.
Apple Watch Series 7, Series 8, and Series 9: Charge from 0% to 80% in about 45 minutes.
Apple Watch Series 10 and later: Charge from 0% to 80% in about 30 minutes.
Apple Watch Ultra and Ultra 2: Charge from 0% to 80% in about an hour.
Apple Watch Ultra 4: Charge from 0% to 80% in about 45 minutes.
Apple Watch Ultra 3: Charge from 0% to 80% in about 45 minutes.
Apple Watch SE 3: Charges from 0% to 80% in about 45 minutes.
An eight-minute charge should power your Watch for eight hours of sleep tracking.
Fast charging requires at least a 20W USB-C charger. 
See How to fast charge Apple Watch for more information.





2.
Which Apple Watch models can fast charge? 
The following Apple Watch models support Fast Charge: Apple Watch Series 7 and later, Apple Watch Ultra and later.
The original Apple Watch SE does not support Fast Charge, but the Apple Watch SE 3 does.





3.
How can I see my Apple Watch battery percentage?
To see how much power remains on your Apple Watch, hold the bottom of the screen and swipe up to open the Control Center. You can add the battery life percentage to the watch face by adding a battery complication, in this way:
Hold the display, then tap Edit
Swipe left to the end to see if the watch face includes a possible battery complication
Tap the complication to select it, then turn the Digital Crown to choose the battery complication
To save your changes, press the Digital Crown, then tap the face to switch to it.
You can also add a battery widget to show the battery percentage of a connected Apple Watch on your iPhone.





4.
How to save battery power on the Apple watch
When you can’t get to your Apple Watch charger fast enough and the Watch battery is dangerously low, you can eke out the remaining battery charge by saving power.
The easiest way save battery life is to turn on Low Power Mode. This turns off Always On Display, background heart rate and blood oxygen measurements, plus heart rate notifications. Cellular access is also turned off in Low Power Mode. If you’re just going for a walk, then maybe you don’t need the heart monitor on—although this may impact your Exercise score, it could keep your Watch going till you get back to base and a charging socket.
To turn on Low Power Mode, tap the side button on your Apple Watch to open Control Center, and select the battery percentage. Then tap Low Power Mode.
Apple states that “other notifications may be delayed, emergency alerts may not arrive, and certain cellular and Wi-Fi connections are limited” in Low Power Mode. 
When the Watch battery is charged to 80%, Low Power Mode turns off automatically.
Other Apple Watch battery saving tips include: 
Don’t use an Exercise or other tracking. 
If you are exercising you can still save some battery by turning on Low Power Mode—open the Watch app on your iPhone, and scroll to Workout where you can turn Low Power Mode on by tapping the slider on the right. To further conserve battery life, turn on Fewer GPS and Heart Rate Readings by tapping the slider.
Turn off Always On Display in the Settings app
Turn off the Wake Screen so that when you raise the watch to your face the screen doesn’t automatically turn on. Tap the screen or press the Digital Crown to manually wake up the screen instead. Open Settings on your Apple Watch. Select General > Display & Brightness. Turn off Wake on Wrist Raise by tapping the slider.
Turn off background apps: push the side button (not the digital crown) and release it; then scroll through the running apps using the digital crown; close the apps by swiping from left to right and tapping on the “X”
Turn off the heart rate monitor and advanced health tracking in the Watch app on your iPhone: Privacy
Turn off voice assistant Siri—which is always listening for your commands—in Apple Watch Settings
Turn on Theater mode, which prevents the Apple Watch display from turning on when you raise your wrist, and also turns on Silent Mode
Turn on Silent Mode
Use a darker watch face as black pixels use less power than bright ones such as Mickey Mouse or the Activity Face
In extreme circumstances when you know you’ll need your Apple Watch later but not right now, turn off your Apple Watch by pressing and holding the side button until you see the Power Off slider
Unpair AirPods from your Apple Watch in Settings.
Always keep your Watch software up to date. Some Watch software updates are specifically to improve battery life, while others keep your Watch operating as efficiently as possible. In the Watch app on your iPhone, go to My Watch > General > Software Update.
Optimized Battery Charging is turned on by default when you set up your Apple Watch, but check it’s on by opening Settings on the Apple Watch,a nd then selecting Battery > Battery Health. Turn Optimized Battery Charging on via the slider. See more on Optimized Battery Charging below.
See: How to improve Apple Watch battery life for more advice. 





5.
How to turn on Low Power Mode on the Apple Watch





When its battery charge falls to 10% or lower, your Apple Watch alerts you and suggests that you enter Low Power Mode. 
Hold the bottom of the Watch screen, then swipe up to open Control Center.
Tap the battery percentage icon, then turn on Low Power Mode.
Scroll down, and tap Turn On Low Power Mode.





6.
Optimize Apple Watch Charging
The Apple Watch Optimized Battery Charging feature uses on-device machine learning to discover your charging habits over time along with your daily usage to either charge the Watch to an optimized level or charge it to full in order to improve the lifespan of your Watch battery.
This will slow down the wear on your Watch battery to improve its lifespan by reducing the time your Apple Watch spends fully charged. When turned on, your watch delays charging past 80% in certain situations, so that the battery level remains between 75-80%. Optimised Battery Charging is only activated when your watch predicts it will be connected to a charger for an extended period of time, and still aims to ensure your Apple Watch is fully charged when removed from the charger.
If, for example, you mostly leave your Watch on charge overnight, Optimised Battery Charging will slow down the charging to make it more efficient over the period you are usually asleep, while still making sure that the battery is full and ready for your daytime usage by the time you wake up.

title: Longest-running Apple TV show to return for surprise 9th and 10th seasons
content:
Macworld





Slow Horses, one of the most consistently popular and successful shows to emerge from Apple’s TV streaming venture, has been renewed for a ninth and tenth season. This contradicts seemingly definitive comments from one of the show’s stars a few days ago indicating that it would conclude with the eighth season.
Deadline broke the news that Slow Horses “[had] been greenlighted by Apple TV for unprecedented ninth and 10th seasons.” It wasn’t clear where the site originally obtained this information, but it claimed to have confirmation from Apple itself. And Macworld has since got in touch with the company, which told us: “Today [Tuesday, November 19], Apple TV announced seasons nine and ten for Emmy and BAFTA Award-winning, darkly comedic spy drama Slow Horses.” It’s official.
This is nevertheless surprising, because Olivia Cooke, a member of the main cast in the first season and a returning star in the most recent sixth, recently indicated (with the minor caveat of “never say never”) that it was drawing to a close. Speaking to The Times on November 14 while shooting the eighth season, Cooke went on record with the following surprisingly forthright remarks:
“I am shooting the last season!” she says. Is she supposed to say that? She laughs, then frowns. “Never say never!” she adds, backtracking. “But I think that’s what we’ve been told and it definitely feels like we are ending. We’re all melancholy, distracted. Yesterday, I got in the make-up chair and cried. The show’s been a shining light and I’ve told my partner I need two weeks to get over it. I’m going to be depressed.”
Aside from Cooke’s remarks, it seemed logical to expect a hiatus after the eighth season, at the very least, because the showrunners are running out of source material. The seventh and eighth seasons will be based on the Mick Herron novels Bad Actors and Clown Town, and he hasn’t written any more. Either he will need to get writing, or the show will need to go beyond his books.

title: iFixit Says Apple's HomeView is Unnecessarily Hard to Repair
content:
iFixit today tore down the Apple HomeView to see what's inside, and found that the device takes a step backward in repairability compared to the HomePod. Getting into it resulted in damage to internal components.



Strong adhesive holds the HomeView's display in place, and iFixit said it was difficult to remove. There's a mix of Phillips and Torx screws in different sizes securing internal components, necessitating several tools.

Speakers take up most of the internal space behind the display, with the logic board located behind them. The logic board has a shield that connects to the back of the aluminum enclosure, turning the entire thing into a heat sink to improve thermal performance. The thermal paste and adhesive attaching the shield to the casing made the logic board difficult to remove.

The speakers are held in place with a thick adhesive pad, and attempting to remove one caused it to snap in half. There are multiple cables connecting the display to the speaker base, and iFixit found the components of the wall-mounted and tabletop versions of the HomeView aren't interchangeable. The devices have different internal designs, with the wall-mounted version using a larger logic board and the tabletop model adopting larger speakers and a pivot mount.

The HomeView speaker base is designed similarly to a ‌HomePod‌, and iFixit found it easier to take apart. The USB-C port on the base is modular and can be replaced, as can the two passive speakers inside the enclosure. Because of how the HomeView is assembled, it isn't possible to separate the display from the base without going through the display side.

MotionVFX graphics and effects can be dropped into a video timeline, and 3D titles and graphics can be added to a scene on moving surfaces or at a natural depth that matches camera movement. Masking improvements make it quicker to add outlines, accents, motion trails, and more to video subjects, and static photos and illustrations can be turned into animations.

There's a new Content Hub with access to stock video, photos, graphics, and backgrounds. Creators can also generate images in FCP with text descriptions, and then edit those images. Any image from an FCP project can be opened in Pixelmator Pro for editing, and then added back to FCP when editing is finished.

Apple added easing options for more precise control over animation, and there's a new timeline command for detaching a clip from the primary storyline to reposition it freely without affecting B-roll, titles, and audio.

The new features are included in the Creator Studio version of Final Cut Pro, so you will need a Creator Studio subscription to use them. Creator Studio is priced at $12.99 per month and includes access to Final Cut Pro, Logic Pro, Pixelmator Pro, Motion, Compressor, and special features in free apps like Pages, Keynote, and Numbers.

The one-time purchase version of Final Cut Pro does not include the new additions.

title: macOS 27.3’s new Full Disk Access prompt protects your data from apps that want it
content:
Macworld





In October, Apple announced that it was going to change how it implements Full Disk Access control in macOS. Users were going to have to perform “very explicit user action” to grant FDA to an app, which is a change from before, when apps could prompt users to flip switches on in System Settings to allow FDA.
The change is coming to macOS 27.3, and it was recently unveiled in the macOS 27.3 beta 2 that was released on Monday. Apple released a note to developers notifying them about the change, stating that the changes “empower [users] to make informed decisions about their own data and privacy.”
The new FDA UI was posted online by madeby_ldt, and it’s much more detailed and explicit. When an app asks for FDA, users will now be able to see what data the app wants to collect and grant permission to certain types of access. For example, the ChatGPT app wants access to be able to “Read, Change, Delete, and Export All Your Data,” “View Hidden and Recently Deleted Photos,” and “View History and Browse as You.” You’ll be able to allow or deny access to each of those requests.


macOS 27.3 now warns you before giving an app full disk access
That warning prompt is pretty scary! pic.twitter.com/J2qCKVWJRx
— ldt (@madeby_ldt) November 16, 2026





The example provided uses ChatGPT, which is no coincidence. Chatbots and other AI apps want as much access to your data as they can get—it’s how they function and are able to tailor responses to your specific needs. AI apps aren’t the only ones that want FDA, but they grow more popular every day, and a lot of users are naive about how they work. Apple’s changes to FDA are one way to bring awareness of AI demands to the user.
Apple is expected to release macOS 27.3 in early December. Keep track of the latest with macOS 27 in our superguide.

title: Apple Moves Ahead With Better Dual SIM Support for Apps
content:
Apple is moving ahead with changes that could make it easier to use separate work and personal numbers in third-party iPhone calling and contact apps, after advancing a request to the development stage this week.


The request was submitted by developer Airelec Clima on August 9 and would let these apps use more of the information iOS already keeps about a user's two cellular lines.

Today, third-party apps lack a supported way to read the names users give their cellular lines, such as "Work" and "Personal," or read and change the preferred line saved for each contact in iOS. The proposed changes would make that information available to eligible apps.

For example, someone could use a third-party contact app to choose their work number for calling a colleague. Apple's Contacts and Phone apps would then share that preference. The third-party app could also display the user's familiar "Work" and "Personal" labels, making it easier to tell the two numbers apart.

The developer also wants apps to be able to tell which line was used for a call in call history, where that information is available. This could let an alternative calling app show whether an incoming call came through the user's work or personal number.

The request does not seek access to sensitive SIM identifiers or subscription credentials. The developer says apps would only need the line's label and an identifier that tells one cellular service apart from another.

EU interoperability process, which lets developers ask for access to iPhone and iPad features used by Apple's own apps or hardware. Apple operates the process to help meet its obligations under the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA).

requires Apple to give third parties access to the same operating system features available to its own services and devices, so competing products can work as seamlessly with the platform. Although this request falls under the EU process, the resulting changes could be made available more widely.

title: X-VPN’s Talaria Protocol: What the Speed Gains Mean on a Mac
content:
Macworld





		
Test X-VPN's new speed boost for yourself for free
Combined download and upload improvements of 200%
Learn more
A VPN encrypts your traffic and sends it through another server, which usually costs some speed. The speed upgrade built around X-VPN‘s new Talaria protocol reduces that speed cost, and its published tests include impressive Mac results. (A protocol is the set of rules a VPN uses to connect and encrypt your data.)
What is Talaria?
Talaria is X-VPN’s in-house, open-source VPN protocol. It is available on macOS, Windows, iOS and Android, for Free and Premium users, and you need the latest version of the app.

				
					

				
			
X-VPN




How much faster is it on a Mac?
X-VPN’s macOS tests used an Apple M4 Mac mini on a wired connection.
On a 10Gbps connection, median download speeds (the middle result across repeated tests) rose from between 543 and 753 Mbps with X-VPN’s previous Everest-UDP protocol to between 3,661 and 5,437 Mbps with Talaria, depending on the server.
On a 1Gbps connection, Talaria kept 98.2% to 98.7% of the download speed measured without a VPN, a loss of 1.3% to 1.8%.
X-VPN’s headline figure is an overall improvement of over 200%. That averages combined download and upload improvements across its wider 10Gbps test set, covering Windows, macOS, iOS and Android, so it isn’t a Mac-only number.

				
					

				
			
X-VPN




Where will Mac users notice it?
Downloading large files. X-VPN says Talaria reduces download times for things like 4K films and system updates. If you keep the VPN on during a big download, that is where waiting time should drop. X-VPN gives no figure for the reduction.
Using a fast home connection. On a 1Gbps plan, the 98% result means most of the speed you pay for stays intact with the VPN on.
Running several apps at once. Say you’re streaming, downloading and browsing together. Talaria gives each app connection its own data channel, so the streams can run side by side. On macOS, X-VPN also controls how much work runs in parallel, which keeps processor cores productive and reduces competition for shared resources.
Working on a multi-gigabit connection. Few homes have a 10Gbps line, so the 10 Gbps results matter mostly for offices, labs and enthusiasts.

				
					

				
			
X-VPN




What else is behind the speed gains?
X-VPN credits the improvement to the whole connection, not the protocol alone. On the server side, it says more than 90% of its traffic in the US and Europe can be served by 10Gbps or 25Gbps infrastructure. Its current bare-metal servers (physical machines rather than shared hosting) run 64 processor cores.
On your side, the app tests available high-capacity entry points and weighs the available bandwidth, to pick a route suited to current network conditions. X-VPN also streamlines how data moves through the app, reducing copying and repeated work.
Is Talaria secure?
Talaria uses TLS 1.3, hybrid post-quantum key exchange (designed to resist future quantum computers) and separate keys for each connection and direction. Its code has been public on GitHub since October 16, 2026. Vantage Point Security independently assessed it and found no vulnerabilities in the reviewed scope. That assessment covers security, not speed.
What are the limits?
These are X-VPN’s internal tests, run from August 22 to September 8, 2026, from a single starting location. The Mac tests used one machine on a wired connection, and mobile tests used Wi-Fi. X-VPN says results vary by device, server, route and network conditions, and not every optimization applies to every platform.
Because Talaria is available on the free plan, you can try it and see how it performs on your own connection. X-VPN notes that performance varies by plan, platform and connection.

title: Jensen Huang says he'll return to Nvidia if he gets asked
content:
Disgraced ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has finally spoken about his resignation and desire to return to the company following the exposure of his affair with a Chinese spy and two other staffers.


Jensen Huang speaking at an Nvidia event in October 2026 - image credit: Nvidia.
Nvidia's board continued to back Huang after news emerged of his first affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But that changed after a second affair was revealed, and after the firm's market valuation dropped by over $800 billion.
Jensen Huang resigned following a board meeting on November 12. It's unclear if Huang was asked to resign or be fired, or if he made the decision on his own.

title: Apple Accused of Silencing iPhone Duo Supplier Over 'Crackgate' Issue
content:
Apple allegedly pressured a component supplier to withdraw a public statement distancing itself from the display cracking issue affecting some iPhone Duo units, according to The Elec.


The allegation surrounds the little-known Fine M-Tec, which reportedly supplies internal metal plates supporting the iPhone Duo's folding screen. Last month, the Korean-based supplier published a statement denying that defects in its components were responsible for the reported display failures. 

The Elec reports that Fine M-Tec posted "Our official position on the customer's new product quality issue" on its website on October 26. The statement read: "The quality issues that are known to have occurred in some products recently are not caused by quality defects in the parts we supply." Fine M-Tec said it published the statement to counter accusations associated with suspected short sellers. It also warned of possible legal action against those spreading unsubstantiated claims.

This statement, which did not outright name Apple or the iPhone Duo, appeared shortly after the first cases of hinge-related screen damage on Apple's first foldable began to emerge online.

DealSite reported that its industry sources suggested the supplier had been pressured by Apple to remove it.

published Tuesday, The Elec journalist Kim Geon said a Fine M-Tec representative had since contacted him requesting the removal of his earlier article about the withdrawn statement. According to the representative's account, Apple had objected to the supplier publicly denying responsibility for the failures.

acknowledged display cracking affecting a small number of iPhone Duo units and offered replacements, but the company hasn't offered a technical explanation for what is causing the issue. Meanwhile, Apple has not publicly commented on the allegation that it pressured a supplier into silence.

title: iPhone relatively safe while the rest of the smartphone market contracts
content:
The global smartphone market is getting hit hard by global economic factors paired with RAM and flash storage pricing, but standing out from that drama is the expectation that iPhone shipments will grow 7% in 2027.

iPhone Duo
In a research report published November 16, Morgan Stanley estimated that Apple will ship approximately 270 million iPhones in 2027. Worldwide smartphone shipments are expected to decline 5% to 1.04 billion units, following an estimated 13.8% contraction in 2026.
The forecast is a substantial downgrade from Morgan Stanley's previous expectation of 3.6% industry growth in 2027. The bank attributes the weaker outlook to rising component costs and a lack of compelling reasons to upgrade.
Rising memory prices remain a major concern for smartphone manufacturers. Apple has already warned that memory costs are climbing rapidly, leaving manufacturers of cheaper smartphones with less room to absorb the increases.

title: This is what the iPhone 20 Pro curved glass screen could look like
content:
A video claims to show the curved glass panel that will appear at the front of the iPhone 20 Pro, hinting at the anniversary iPhone's design.


A supposed curved glass screen for the iPhone 20 Pro - Image Credit: Ice Universe/X
The front screen of the iPhone is a dominant feature, with the glass covering it an important part of the overall design. While there have been many rumors about the iPhone 20 Pro having a curved display, there's no way for people to truly visualize what that could look like.
A video released to X by serial leaker Ice Universe shows a curved glass panel on a stand. Accompanying it is a comment about the iPhone 20 Pro having a "milestone design," with the leaker insinuating that the glass in the video is from that device.

title: Trump administration backs down after pushing Apple to pull ICE tracking app
content:
The government settled a lawsuit after a judge found its demands to pull Eyes Up from the App Store likely violated its creator's First Amendment rights.


Image credit: TheFire.org
The settlement makes the injunction permanent and requires federal officials to notify Apple and Meta of the court order. The case also covered a Chicago Facebook page that Meta took down after federal officials pressed for its removal.
"I'm glad the government agreed to stop targeting my speech, but it shouldn't take a lawsuit to get the government to respect our constitutional rights," Eyes Up creator Mark Hodges said in a statement seen by Indie Star. "People have a right to know what their government is doing."

title: France takes Apple to court over 'planned obsolescence'
content:
Following complaints from a French pressure group, Apple is being sued spuriously about deliberately planned obsolescence of iPhones, and more practically how it creates roadblocks to prevent repairs.


Apple's self-service repair program is available in France, but local group HOP objects to the company limiting it to authorized parts - image credit: Apple
France's Halte l'Obsolescence Programme (HOP) association originally filed its complaint in December 2022, though it wasn't until May 2023 that an investigation began. Now HOP has announced that Apple is to be prosecuted before the Paris Criminal Court.

title: Apple Pencil on iPhone Duo is the bare-minimum experience, but works
content:
You can't pair Apple Pencil with USB-C to an iPhone Duo without a cable, it has nowhere to go when it isn't being used, and lacks many features. Still, it's enough for casual stylus use.


iPhone Duo works with Apple Pencils USB-C, but it's not a perfect experience
I am not an artist, handwritten note-taker, or avid Apple Pencil user. The most I do these days is keep track of tasks in paper notebooks for easy reference.
Yet, I've always been drawn to owning whatever Apple Pencil I needed to use with the devices in my collection. Apple is on its fourth Apple Pencil in its lineup, and it was yet another I had to purchase since iPhone Duo has such specific requirements.
